PREFACE
I, the Chairman of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Science and
Technology, Environment and Forests, having been authorised by the Committee to present the
Report on its behalf, present this One Hundred and Ninety-fifth Report on the Action Taken by the
Department of Science and Technology on the recommendations contained in One Hundred and
Eighty-fifth Report of the Committee on Demands for Grants (2008-09) of the Department of
Science and Technology.
2. The Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Department of Science and
Technology on the recommendations contained in the One Hundred and Eighty-fifth Report of the
Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Science and Technology, Environment and
Forests on the Demands for Grants (2008-09) of the Department of Science and Technology which
was presented to the Rajya Sabha on 29th April, 2008.
3. There were twenty-sixth recommendations contained in the One Hundred and Eighty-fifth
Report of the Committee. Action Taken Notes on the recommendations of the Committee were
received from the Department on 21st August, 2008.
4. In the meeting held on 13th October, 2008 the Committee considered the draft Action Taken
Report and adopted the same.
DR. V . MAITREYAN
N
EW D ELHI; Chairman,
October 13, 2008 Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on
Science and Technology, Environment and Forests.

1
REPORT
The report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Department of Science and
Technology on the recommendations contained in the One hundred and Eighty-fifth Report of the
Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Science and Technology, Environment and
Forests on the Demands for Grants (2008-09) of the Department of Science and Technology,
which was presented to both the Houses of Parliament on 29th April, 2008. There were twenty-
six recommendations in the One hundred and Eighty-fifth Report of the Committee. Action Taken
notes on the recommendations of the Committee were received from the Department on
21st August, 2008.
Recommendation (Para 2.2)
The Committee has been informed that the Department’s plan outlay of Rs. 1526 crores at
the BE stage last year was reduced to Rs.1270 crores at the RE stage. The Department, however,
was unable to spend even the reduced Grants during the last year. The Committee takes serious
note of the situation and recommends that the Department should be more prompt and efficient in
utilising the allocated funds. This acquires even more importance because the rise in allocation this
year, the Committee feels, is miniscule, if put in the context of inflation and economic growth. At
the same time the Committee is of the opinion that, keeping in mind the responsibilities of the
Department and the role it is expected to play in development of science and technology, the
Department should be given an increase in allocation in consonance with its requirements.
Action Taken by the Government
It is a fact that Department of Science and Technology Plan outlay was Rs.1526 crore at
the BE stage. This was reduced to Rs.1270 crore at the RE stage. Accounts for the financial year
2007-08 are under process. As per the provisional figures, expenditure of Rs.1266.18 crore took
place during financial year 2007-08. This amounts to 99.70 per cent of the budget provided at the
RE stage. The Department has successfully utilized the reduced budget at the RE stage.
Comments
The Committee expresses its concern that the funds allocated remained underutilized
leading to a reduction at RE stage in the last financial year and is of the opinion that a
comprehensive introspection by the department is required, to find out the reasons for the
under utilization and taking corrective measures to avoid such a recurrence in this financial
year.
Recommendation (Para 4.2)
The Committee welcomes the constitution of Expert Advisory Committees to monitor and
review the progress of its ongoing schemes and is of the opinion that such a step can be helpful
in prioritization and rationalisation of schemes.
Action Taken by the Government
Scientific Engineering Research Council: The Department has constituted several Expert
Advisory Committees in various areas of Science and Engineering. These Expert Committees advise
the Department in the formulation of guidelines for receiving and processing research proposals for

2
support under the scheme; the suitability and extent of grant for research programmes; make
suitable recommendations on the choice of discipline and specific fields which need increased
support for research and evaluate the progress of each research programme supported by it and
make suitable recommendations regarding its continuation or otherwise.
Survey of India (SOI): has formulated a review/monitoring committee under the
Chairmanship of Surveyor General of India wherein the progress of each and every plan schemes
is being monitored regularly.
The activities under various plan schemes, the target of which have been met/have been
concluded, have been taken out from the schemes. The available schemes have been reprioritized
as per the availability of annual plan fund. In order to continue the on-going schemes for which
budget is not available, the funds for the same are being projected in RE.
As regards the National Training Programme for Scientists/Technologists working with
Government of India, the comments of the Committee have been noted.
Drug and Pharma Research Programme, Technology Systems Group Programme, Instrument
Development Programme and Water T echnology Initiatives: The Expert Committees have been formed
for monitoring and reviewing the progress of these schemes in line with the recommendations of the
Committee. These Committees are constituted for a specific period to guide and monitor the schemes.
Science and Technology Entrepreneurship Development: All the projects under Science and
Technology Entrepreneurship Development scheme are implemented with the guidance of Expert
Advisory Committees. The guidance of the respective Committees is taken by the Department in
prioritization and rationalization of various programmes under the said scheme.
Science and Technology Communication: The programmes of Science and Technology
Communication will be reviewed through a Committee of experts as recommended by the
Department related Parliamentary Standing Committee. The review will be useful in drawing up
areas for intervention on priority and bringing more focus to the efforts.
Technology Development Board: The Government of India constituted the Technology
Development Board (TDB) in September 1996 under the Technology Development Board Act, 1995.
As per the TDB Act, the Board has 11 members consisting of 6 Secretaries to the Government
of India who are in charge of:—
(1) Department of Science and T echnology Chairperson
(2) Department of Scientific and Industrial Research ex-Officio Member
(3) Department of Defence Research and Development ex-Officio Member
(4) Department of Industrial Development ex-Officio Member
(5) Department of Rural Development ex-Officio Member
(6) Department of Expenditure (Finance) ex-Officio Member
The Board has upto 4 nominated members from persons having experience in technology
development and application, banking and finance, industry, agriculture and rural development. It
has a Secretary to the Board as a member.
TDB constitutes Committees as per its requirements.
Comments
The Committee appreciates the steps taken by the Department and hopes that it will
lead to speedy implementation of various schemes.

3
Recommendation (Para 7.2 and 7.3)
The Secretary of the Department during the presentation made to the Committee has
informed that Science and Engineering Research Council (SERC) needs an increase in allocation of
about 25 per cent in order to fulfill its objectives. The Committee, keeping in mind the huge array
of responsibilities for promotion of research in newly emerging and frontier areas of science and
engineering including multidisciplinary fields; need for encouraging young scientists to take up
challenging R&D activities and imperatives to promote basic and applied research in frontline areas
of engineering and technology in various academic and research institutions, etc., among many
others, recommends that sufficient budgetary support may be provided so that the programme
could be pursued with vigour.
The Committee has been informed that around 3000 research proposals are received by the
Department every year out of which 500-600 proposals are selected for funding. The Committee
is of the view that lack of fund should not be allowed to come in the way of funding good and
promising research proposals.
Action Taken by the Government
A Plan allocation (BE) of Rs. 415.0 crore has been made for Research and Development
Support (SERC) scheme in 2008-09 as against the previous financial year’s of Rs.344.0 crore
(BE). The support to research is enhanced by creating increased and expanded knowledge in basic
research, excellence in science and engineering, innovation and promotion of selected areas,
encouragement for industrial partnership in projects under engineering and technology, training of
manpower and encouragement to young scientists. A number of fellowships; like, Ramanna
Fellowship for performing scientists, Ramanujan Fellowships to attract outstanding scientists and
engineers from all over the world to take up scientific research in our country; and J.C Bose
Fellowships to recognize and support active, performing Indian scientists and engineers, would be
instituted in 2008-09.
The SERC of the Department has emerged as the single largest support system engaged in
promoting basic research in all areas of science and engineering and has achieved significant
success in furthering the growth of research in new inter-disciplinary areas in science and
engineering. SERC has been considered as the highest standard of Peer-Review and transparent
mechanism in promoting R&D across ‘disciplines’ and ‘institutions’. There is a genuine need of
enhancing the critical mass of scientists with quality. The Department has planned several
innovative methods to enhance the number to meet the rising challenges ahead. Programmes for
elevating group dynamics through special initiatives, mentoring, etc., are some of the immediate
steps for enhancing the number with quality. Through ‘mentoring’ the expertise and experience of
a large number of retired and near retiring scientists could be utilized. It targets an augmentation
initiative for such proposals which fall short of the required benchmark by a narrow margin. At
present, there is no constraint for funding good and promising research proposals.
Comments
The Committee is of the opinion that the present generation should be motivated
through various incentives to take up research in frontier areas of science and, therefore,
reiterates that adequate budgetary support be provided so that funds shortage does not
come in the way of promising research proposals.
Recommendation (Para 8.3)
The success of Science can be gauged by the fact as to how far it has been able to touch

4
and ameliorate the life and lot of one and all. The Committee feels that going by this yardstick a
lot more is desired to be done. The Committee is of the opinion that science should come out of
the confines of laboratories to make its outreach to the common masses and it needs to be done
in a time bound manner or a sustained basis. This becomes all the more imperative as India needs
to shed its tag of a developing nation and acquire the stature of a developed one, the sooner the
better, and it is none other but science which holds the magic stick to do wonders. DST being
the nodal Ministry, the onus lies with it. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the
Department of Science and Technology should coordinate with all other scientific departments and
institutions to move forward in this direction and lay more and more emphasis on S&T programme
for socio-economic development.
Action Taken by the Government
The Department of Science and Technology (DST) has good mechanism for coordinating
with other scientific departments and institutions for developing and implementing S&T
programmes for socio-economic development. For example, representatives of such departments/
institutions are members of Expert Advisory Committee and they also help DST in monitoring the
progress of such programmes.
Comments
The Committee emphasises the need for proper coordination among various agencies
involved, so as to ensure that there is no duplication and wastage of resources in achieving
the same goal.
Recommendation (Para 9.4 and 9.5)
The Committee acknowledges the important role that Technology Development Programmes
(TDP) plays in translating lab-scale research into technology mode but for which the benefit of
science cannot be reaped. The Committee, therefore, desires that Technology Development
Programmes should be further strengthened and intensified so that the advantages of new
breakthroughs in the field of science could be taken to the masses at the earliest and at an
affordable cost.
The Committee is also of the view that developing indigenous technology through joint
projects is also of utmost importance because without industry participation such projects will not
only become exorbitant but also lack the commercial dimension which is very important for
successful culmination of such projects.
Action Taken by the Government
The recommendations of the Committee have been taken note of. In this connection, it is
mentioned that the Technology Development Board is the first organization of its kind within the
Government framework with the sole objective of translating the fruits of indigenous research into
commercial products or services.
The Board plays a pro-active role by encouraging commercial enterprises to take up
technology oriented projects.
Technology Development Board aims at accelerating the development and commercialisation
of indigenous technology or adapting imported technology to wider domestic application. The board
provides financial assistance in the form of equity, soft loans or grants.

5
Comments
The Committee appreciates the initiative taken by the department to set up the
‘Technology Development Board’ which is a first of its kind to take research out from the
confines of the laboratories and bring it within the reach of common man. The Committee
feels that such initiatives should be pursued with renewed vigour.
Recommendation (Para 10.3)
The Committee is of the view that the mapping work should not suffer as a result of
inadequacy of funds, as it plays an important role in planning of resource utilization and other schemes.
Action Taken by the Government
The budgetary allocation for  the scheme Modernization of Mapping Organisations
(Survey of India — SOI and National Atlas and Thematic Mapping Organisation — NATMO) during
2008-09 is only marginally lower than 2007-08. As per fund and work requirement, additional
allocation will be made available at the RE stage.
Comments
The Committee hopes that the mapping work progresses as per schedule set by the
Department.
Recommendation (Para 11.5)
The Committee has been informed that DST plans to initiate five autonomous S&T
institutions in areas of glaciology, molecular materials, pre-competitive research institute for
computer sciences, etc., where India would require R&D capacities and need for  National initiatives
for R&D in these areas have been felt. The Committee recommends that the process of
establishment of five autonomous Science and Technology institutions in different fields be
expedited so as to ensure that they become operational within the stipulated period and become
ready to meet the demands and expectations of these areas. The Committee also recommends that
impact assessment study of other institutions on the lines of National Accreditation Board for
Laboratories (NABL) and Technology Information, Forecasting, Assessment Council (TIF AC) may
also be undertaken so as to suitably restructure to derive maximum results out of them.
Action Taken by the Government
DST is in the process of initiating the take over/establishment of various institutes and
converting them as autonomous grant-in-aid institutions of the Government of India under the
Department of Science and Technology and making them national level institutes.
Comments
The Committee hopes that more number of national institutes to undertake research
in high technology areas be established.
Recommendation (Para 12.3)
The Committee recommends enhancing allocations for the project at the RE stage because
such a strategic project which has a catalytic effect on very important R&D and technology
development projects involving multiple agencies needs more funds for cutting-edge research.

6
Action Taken by the Government
Office of the Principal Scientific Adviser to the Government of India proposes to request
Department of Science and Technology to suitably enhance the allocation for Synergy Projects at
RE (2008-09) stage.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.
Recommendation (Para 13.5)
The Committee welcomes the initiative of the Department to upgrade the skills of its
scientists by conducting various training programmes which will certainly enable them to meet
contemporary standards and overcome any difficulties arising out of lack of training. The
Committee recommends that more funds may be provided by the Government at RE stage so that
some more training programmes may be added under this scheme.
Action Taken by the Government
The Department is in the process of finalisation of 2 additional training programmes on
‘Energy Security and Management and Impact of Globlisation in the perspective of Indian Science
and Technology’ to be conducted at NIAS, Bangalore. Additional Budget for these programmes
would be considered at R.E. stage in case savings are available subject to approval of Ministry of
Finance.
Comments
The Committee is of the opinion that in the context of continuous inventions and
development of new technologies, skills upgradation of the scientist through training
programmes is an urgent need and, therefore, sufficient funds must be allocated for the
purpose.
Recommendation (Para 14.3)
The Committee is of the view that in a country where poverty is rampant and substantial
part of population suffers from diseases, a continued effort in drug research is required for
providing cheaper medicines. Continued support to drug research programmes should be provided
to enable the scientists to find cheaper and effective drugs. The Committee recommends that drug
research programmes should focus on diseases which are afflicting the large populace of our
country.
Action Taken by the Government
Drugs and Pharmaceuticals Research Programme (DPRP) of DST invariably gives
importance for the R&D proposals relating to developing cheaper and effective new drugs on
diseases; such as, Tuberculosis, Malaria, Dengue, Diarrhoea, Kala-Azar, Diabetes, HIV/AIDS,
Asthma, Arthritis, Osteoporosis, Japanese Encephalitis, Amoebiasis, which are afflicting the large
population in the country. In addition, in line with the recommendation of the Committee, the
Government has approved providing grants-in-aid to Indian pharmaceutical industry for R&D
projects involving clinical trials (Phase I, II and III) to develop new drugs for neglected diseases;
such as, tuberculosis, malaria, kala-azar, filariasis, etc. The Indian pharma industry would thus be
able to develop effective and cheaper drugs for poorer society of our country.

7
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and hopes that drug research programmes would be
expedited.
Recommendation (Para 14.5)
The Committee reiterates it earlier recommendation that more efforts should be made to
make alternative system of medicines successfully fill in the gap in areas where conventional cures
are not available. The Committee felt that research in traditional/alternative systems should focus
on areas where conventional cures are either inadequate or too costly.
Action Taken by the Government
The Drugs and Pharmaceuticals Research Programme (DPRP), since its inception during
1994-95, up to March 2008, had forged 88 industry institutional collaborative R&D projects for
drug development on various diseases which include 32 projects in traditional/alternative systems.
In addition, 36 national facilities for the benefit of pharma industry including industries of
traditional and alternative systems have been established in different universities/national
laboratories. The programme has extended 40 soft loans to pharma industries to undertake R&D
projects for drug development. The treatment for diseases like Psoriasis, Leucoderma, HIV/AIDS
and Rheumatoid Arthritis is either costly or inadequate in allopathic system of medicines. Research
projects have been covered under traditional system of medicines to develop drugs for such
diseases. The Committee’s recommendation is noted to give thrust in such areas.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.
Recommendation (Para 15.4)
The Committee welcomes the proposal to establish three major Institutes of Nano Science
and Technology and the introduction of PG Teaching Programmes (M.Sc./M.Tech.) in Nano
Science and Technology. The Committee is of the view that such proactive steps are required for
creating a pool of scientists to cater to the needs of this unfolding research frontier which holds
immense potential for the future.
Action Taken by the Government
The Department has put in all efforts for realizing these three Institutes of Nano Science
and Technology (INST) as early as possible in the country. The proposal of INST, Mohali has been
approved by the Expenditure Finance Committee (EFC). Presently, it has been referred to Cabinet
for concurrence. The other two proposals are at the EFC stage. PG Teaching Programmes in Nano
Science and Technology (NST) and Postdoctoral Fellowships in NST are progressing well in terms
of quality and quantity.
Comments
The Committee desires that administrative delays should be avoided and the three
institutes may be established at the earliest.
Recommendation (Para 16.3)
The Committee appreciates the scheme and is of the view that the above programme is a

8
step taken in right direction and more such programmes are required to initiate and retain students
in the field of science. The Committee feels that funds should not be allowed to be an obstacle
as the future of science and of the country rests on such small beginnings which will have crucial
effects on the future.
Action Taken by the Government
The Department would take all necessary steps for early implementation of the Innovation
in Science Pursuit for Inspired Research (INSPIRE) scheme including Scholarships for Science in
Higher Education (SHE).
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and hopes that this scheme would boost the interest
of the new generation towards science and therefore must be expedited.
Recommendation (Para 16.4)
The Committee feels that the geographical reach of Science in Higher Education (SHE)
should also be extended to distant parts ofthe country like Ladakh and the Northeast and other
backward states. The Committee has also been informed that the Department was unable to
implement the ‘SHE’ scheme because it required consultation and approval of several departments.
The Committee recommends that the Department expedite the process of consultation along with
other Departments for speedy execution of proposals. Beside this the Committee also recommends
that a special effort should be made to increase the reach of the programmes to students who are
not as advantaged as in the Metros but are equally deserving and this should specially take into
consideration girl students who are unable to take advantage of opportunities.
Action Taken by the Government
The Department has carried out extensive national consultation, including with the state
educational bodies. Selections of students are being made by taking proportionally uniform
distribution among various States, including Ladakh, the Northeast and other backward states. The
EFC approved the SHE component and it is at final stages of approval by the Government. The
EFC memos for other components are at appraisal stage. The scheme would be announced in
electronic as well as in print media for wider dissemination. All efforts would be made to reach
the rural areas primarily through regional, local media/newspapers. Preliminary data studies show
that girl students have outnumbered the boys for the proposed fellowship.
Comments
The Committee appreciates the fact that the department has given due consideration
to the underprivileged students from the far flung and backward states of the country and
hopes that in future the scheme would receive wider popularization.
Recommendation (Para 17.4)
In the light of the serious crunch in availability of quality scientists, schemes like INSPIRE
along with other such schemes need constant focus and attention. Scheme for Early Attracting of
Talents for Science (SEATS) and Assured Opportunity for Research Careers (AORC) in the age
group of 22-32 years for 5 years doctoral research backed by an assured research career
opportunity scheme for a another period of five years after their Ph. D in sciences are well-thought

9
schemes which if properly implemented have the potential to meet the intended targets and the
Committee therefore, feels that these schemes should be given the required attention.
Action Taken by the Government
The Department has noted the recommendations by the Committee. As recommended, the
Department is confident that the implementation of INSPIRE with its components SEATS and
AORC, which is presently at the EFC stage, would widen and strengthen the research base in the
country and would help reduce the gap between requirements of quality human resource and its
supply.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and hopes that the department would be successful
in implementation of the scheme.
Recommendation (Para 17.5)
The Committee is of the view that the Department should prioritize its activities and focus
on its core competencies rather than spreading its resources too thin. The top-most priority should
be given to tapping young talent through various monetary and motivational schemes. Stress should
be laid on ‘catching them young’.
Action Taken by the Government
Developing and nurturing of human resource in Science and Technology has always been
on top of the Department’s agenda. A number of ongoing schemes have been strengthened to
attract research scholars; namely, Young Scientists/Women Scientists Fellowships; Swarnajayanthi
Fellowships and J.C. Bose and Ramanujam Fellowships for practicing scientists, Junior/Senior
Research Fellowships (JRF/SRF), etc. More recently, the fellowships of JRF/SRF have been
enhanced. INSPIRE and SHE are two noticeable and significant steps towards ‘catching them
young’.
Comments
The Committee hopes that the scheme would be able to achieve its objectives of
attracting more and more research scholars and thereby provide much needed scientific
manpower.
Recommendation (Para 18.4 and 18.5)
The Committee is of the opinion that a project for development of low cost filters for
domestic purposes should be given top-most priority as millions of households in this country, for
want of affordable filters, suffer from waterborne diseases. Integrating effective technologies to
purify drinking water supplied by civic authorities is yet another challenge to be taken by the
Department in larger interest. The Committee would also like the Department to enter into
partnership with Industry so as to make such products commercial and popular.
The Committee is also of the opinion that such water treatment technology should be made
available in large scale catering to the needs at community level and arsenic, fluoride, iron and other
hazardous minerals should be removed before it reaches households. The Committee is of the
further view that there is an urgent need to develop models which would be low cost, low power
consuming and which can benefit people of different parts of the country afflicted by the problem.

10
Action Taken by the Government
In line with the opinion of the Committee, DST has initiated a project, to be jointly
implemented by Institute of Mineral and Materials Technology (IMMT), Bhubaneshwar, Central
Institute of Plastic Engineering and Technology (CIPET), Chennai and concerned states, under
which terafil water filters would be manufactured with the help of local entrepreneurs/NGOs for
large scale demonstrations in 5 States. These would enhance the confidence of the manufacturers
for commercializing the technology.
The Department has taken initiative to set up community based plants for removal of iron,
arsenic, dissolved salts, etc., from water for providing safe drinking water to the community. In
addition to the 16 such plants as mentioned earlier in the Demand for Grants (2008-2009), 15 more
plants have been sanctioned for setting up in the State of Nagaland for iron removal. The
demonstration of the low cost house hold filter or arsenic removal has been initiated in the Balia
Distt., UP in addition to the earlier demonstration made in all the homes of the village Lalmath in
Nadia Distt., West Bengal.
Comments
The Committee hopes that the implementation and commercialization of the water
purification and water treatment technology would receive adequate support from the
department, so that pure and safe drinking water may be supplied across the country.
Recommendation (Para 19.3)
The Committee is of the opinion that an innovation infrastructure to link knowledge
products to the generation of wealth is of immense importance in knowledge economy. Rich
fruits of research should also be commercially viable to sustain themselves and encourage
further research. Innovation clusters benefiting the academy and industrial sectors under an
effective public-private partnership model is the need of the hour for future successes of research
initiatives.
Action Taken by the Government
Necessary approval for implementation of the Innovation Clusters scheme during the
Eleventh Five Year Plan has been obtained. As recommended by the Committee various models
under Public Private Partnership would be tried during the implementation of the scheme.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.
Recommendation (Para 20.3)
The convergence of technology and security issues is indicative of the highly technological
world we are living in. Technology not only determines how we live our lives but also how we
protect ourselves from negative forces determined to destroy our social and economic fabric. It
is here that the Committee feels that technology has an important role to play in intelligence
gathering as well as monitoring internal security situation and it urges that the Department should
do all that is possible to achieve breakthroughs in security technology in a time bound manner so
that we could be in a position to effectively tackle the threats posed to our internal security and
improve our intelligence gathering capabilities.

11
Action Taken by the Government
Since Security Technology is a new scheme which is being introduced in the Eleventh Five
Year Plan, necessary approvals are being sought for implementation of the scheme. The
recommendations of the Parliamentary Standing Committee are well taken by the Department. The
Department would try its level best to achieve some fruitful results as outcome of this scheme to
effectively tackle the threats posed to our security.
Comments
The Committee is of the view that technology plays an important role in the
protection of society from divisive forces and hence recommends that ‘Security Technology’
scheme should be accorded top priority.
Recommendation (Para 21.4)
The Committee welcomes the symbiotic research initiative taken by the Department along with
Department of Atomic Energy (DAE). Identification of areas where an effective partnership of the
two departments can bring about an effective capacity building in the university and academic sector
for building mega faculties for basic research is of utmost importance as it is a known fact that
without progress in basic science, technological progress cannot sustain itself for very long.
Action Taken by the Government
The Department has noted the recommendations by the Committee. The EFC memorandum
is at final stages of approval.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and hopes that the department will explore other
avenues of cooperation and partnership with other agencies in the area of research.
Recommendation (Para 21.5)
The Committee has been informed that the Department has developed a soil-testing kit,
which costs Rs.3000 per unit. The Committee would like the Department to popularise the kit
among farmers and rope in Industry to promote the product. The Committee also recommends that
the Department should coordinate with the Ministry of Agriculture to promote its uses among the
farmers. It also recommends that at least one soil testing kit be made available free of cost at the
Panchayat or Village, level so that even small and marginal farmers, who otherwise can’t afford
to purchase it, are not deprived of its benefits.
Action Taken by the Government
In accordance with the recommendations of the Parliamentary Standing Committee, efforts
are being made to coordinate with the Ministry of Agriculture for promoting the use of Soil Testing
Kit among the farmers and also making available the kit at Panchayat Level. Other avenues for
promoting the use of Soil Testing Kit among the farmers are also being explored.
Comments
The Committee hopes that the soil testing kit would be popularized and made
available to farmers across the country.

12
Recommendation (Para 22.2)
The Committee is of the view that the ‘Science Express’ programme of the Department has
shown encouraging results and should be further intensified and expanded to the rural and
backward areas of the country. There is need for better monitoring of the programme for crowd
management and more such expresses should be introduced so that viewers get more time while
viewing.
Action Taken by the Government
In light of the recommendation, we are working on modifying the exhibits in the Science
Express and scheduling an itinerary to cover rural and backward areas of the country. The
platforms will have better arrangements for managing the visitors and television monitors will be
installed to screen science films to utilize the waiting period of the visitors. Longer halts will ensure
viewers get more time inside the exhibition. The second phase will commence this winter (October-
November, 2008) and will have about 50 halts.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and hopes that the science popularisation schemes
such as “Science Express” may be given adequate financial support.
Recommendation (Para 23.2)
After considering the Demands for Grants of the Department of Science and Technology
assessing the progress of various important programmes and projects administered by it, the
Committee recommends that the budgetary allocation of Rs. 1780.00 crores under Demand No. 83
(Department of Science and Technology) as sought by the Department for the year 2008-09 may
be approved.
Action Taken by the Government
Department of Science and Technology has been allocated budget of Rs.1530 crore under
Demand No. 83 for the financial year 2008-09. There is gap of Rs.250 crore in regard to the
recommendation of the Parliamentary Standing Committee to provide budget of Rs.1780 crore.
Additional funds will be sought at the RE stage, if the level of expenditure is significant and the
requirements of more funds for the various schemes of the department is justified.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.

13
MINUTES

14

15

PREFACE
I, the Chairman of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Science and
Technology, Environment and Forests, having been authorised by the Committee to present the
Report on its behalf, present this One Hundred and Ninety-sixth Report on the Action Taken by
the Department of Bio-technology on the recommendations contained in the One Hundred and
Ninetieth Report of the Committee on Demands for Grants (2008-09) of the Department of Bio-
technology.
2. The Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Department of Bio-
technology on the recommendations contained in the One Hundred and Ninetieth Report of the
Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Science and Technology, Environment and
Forests on the Demands for Grants (2008-09) of the Department of Bio-technology which was
presented to the Rajya Sabha on 29th April, 2008.
3. There were sixteen recommendations contained in the One Hundred and Ninetieth Report of
the Committee. Action Taken Notes on the recommendations of the Committee were received from
the Department on 16th September, 2008.
4. In the meeting held on 13th October, 2008 the Committee considered the draft Action Taken
Report and adopted the same.
DR. V . MAITREYAN
N
EW D ELHI; Chairman,
October 13, 2008 Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on
Science and Technology, Environment and Forests.

1
REPORT
The Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Department of Bio-
technology on the recommendations contained in the One hundred and Ninetieth Report of the
Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Science and Technology, Environment and
Forests on the Demands for Grants (2008-09) of the Department of Bio-technology, which was
presented to both the Houses of Parliament on 29th April, 2008. There were sixteen recommendations
in the One Hundred Ninetieth Report of the Committee. Action Taken notes on the recommendations
of the Committee were received from the Department on 16th September, 2008.
RECOMMENDATION (PARA 3.2)
The Committee is of the opinion that the Department should be provided with additional
fund at the RE stage so that the gap between the projected demand and the actual allocation can
be bridged so as to enable the Department to establish new autonomous institutions. The committee
is also of the view that the well thought out projected demands of scientific departments should
be honored and accepted by the planning commission, more so when the department has the
capacity and the readiness to utilize the additional funds.
Action Taken by the Government
The recommendation of the Committee was brought to the notice of Planning Commission
during Annual Performance Review meeting held in April, 2008. The Planning Commission assured
provision of additional funds at the RE stage depending upon the progress of expenditure.
Comments
The Committee hopes that the Department would pursue with the Planning
Commission for providing additional funds at RE stage and expects that in future atleast the
scientific departments would be spared from routine cuts in funds allocation as they are
responsible for the country’s technological progress.
RECOMMENDATION (PARA 3.3)
The Committee also strongly recommends that the Department should draw a reasonable
time frame for establishing new autonomous institutions and devise a mechanism to monitor their
progress periodically so as to avoid time and cost overruns.
Action Taken by the Government
During the Eleventh Plan, establishment of 8 new institutions in frontier areas of
biotechnology have been taken up. Out of this, approvals from Expenditure Finance Committee
(EFC) and Cabinet have been already obtained in case of 3 institutions and implementation of
activities has already begun. EFCs have been circulated in case of 2 other institutions for comments
and the same are under preparation in case of 2 more institutions. Further, the Cabinet Note for
establishment of UNESCO centre is in pipeline as per procedure. In all these cases, the timeline
for implementation are clearly worked out for monitoring from time to time.
Comments
The Committee feels that administrative delays should be avoided by the Department
in the establishment of new scientific institutions.

2
RECOMMENDATION (PARA 3.5)
The Committee is pleased to know that the current trend of expenditure indicates that there
are no budget heads of the schemes under which the funds will be underutilized. The Committee
is of the opinion that the Department should continue its good efforts for optimum utilization of
funds.
Action Taken by the Government
The department notes the appreciation made by the committee and sincere efforts will be
made to maintain the trend.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.
RECOMMENDATION (PARA 3.7)
The Committee desires that the reorientation of some of the above programmes, which
could not be completed, should be given a sharper focus and more efforts should be made for their
completion so as to avoid wastage of scarce resource owing to unnecessary delays.
Action Taken by the Government
The programmes dropped during the Tenth Plan have completed the objectives, then set for
their project duration. One of the schemes namely ‘Biotech product and process development’ has
been reoriented with a sharp focus based ‘on the research trends /leads and is being implemented
during Eleventh Plan as a scheme “Bio-processing and Scale-up”.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.
RECOMMENDATION (PARA 3.9)
The Committee is pleased to know that the Department has been successful in meeting its
targets set for the Tenth Plan. Growth rate of 40% is encouraging and thus the Committee desires
that the Department should continue the good work during the next plan period also.
Action Taken by the Government
The Department noted the appreciations of the committee and efforts will be made to
maintain the trend.
Comments
The Committee hopes that the targets for the future plans would also be met
successfully.
RECOMMENDATION (PARA 4.5)
The Committee is of the view that remodeling/ reengineering of university departments of
Life Sciences is of utmost importance in order to remain globally competitive. The Committee
expresses its concern over the lack of infrastructure for R&D in molecular modeling, protein

3
engineering, drug designing, immunological studies, pre-clinical studies, clinical trials, etc. as
without a strong R&D base success of Department will remain short-term and would fail to
sustain, itself in the long run. Therefore, the Committee recommends that infrastructure for R&D
needs to be built up adequately to achieve the desired targets fixed in the Eleventh Plan period.
Action Taken by the Government
Keeping in view the observations of the Committee, the department had advertised the
scheme inviting proposals from universities on certain parameters of reengineering of Life Science
departments. About 12 universities responded with letter of intents. The process of selection for
funding and support is ongoing based on the merit of the proposal and vision of the university to
transform life science research for making it globally competitive. Department will support every
effort made in upgrading the infrastructure of R&D base of Life Sciences Department in such
universities.
Comments
The Committee is of the opinion that the department should strive towards the
upgradation of research and development facilities both at the graduate and undergraduate
levels.
RECOMMENDATION (PARA 5.2)
The Committee is of the opinion that State Agriculture University should be given required
support to start interdisciplinary translational research centres so as to emerge as solution providers
for local agricultural needs. The Committee recommends that the Department engages itself in
exploring the possibilities for the use of barren land for agricultural or horticultural purposes with
the help of bio-technology, as this would help bring a vast unutilized area under productive
cultivation in the country.
The Committee would be happy to see progress in potential application of
nano-biotechnology in agriculture, medicine and environment.
Special emphasis needs to be paid for use of technology in preserving our environment
which has seen large scale degradation. This would go a long way in conservation of lakes which
are getting polluted every day.
The Committee would also like the Department to establish specialized virus research
centres to address viral biology, pathogenesis, biomarkers, etc. within a reasonable time-period.
Action Taken by the Government
The Department has evolved a scheme to support State Agriculture Universities strengthen
research in interdisciplinary areas. Four agriculture universities have been provided programme
based support for the purpose. Dialogue with more agriculture universities through site visits by
experts have been undertaken for assisting them to prepare suitable proposals. To address the needs
of the degraded lands with the salinity, alkalinity and heavy metal toxicity, several programmes have
been undertaken for developing crops resistant to these abiotics factors. Several leads are already
available.
The Department during Eleventh plan has a separate allocation for promoting the application
of nano-technology in agriculture, medicine and environment. So far, about 70 translational R&D
proposals have been approved for implementation for a period of 3-5 years. A special experts
committee has been constituted for technical appraisal and review. Opportunities for utilizing the

4
research leads in these programmes through public-private partnerships have also been put in place
through separate schemes and mechanisms.
The Department has a major programme with separate budgetary allocation and special
expert Task Force for addressing problems of environmental degradation and biodiversity
conservation. Six thrust areas have been identified namely biodegradation of Hazardous pollutants;
bioremediation of polluted sites as well as degraded eco-system; biopolymers/biodegradable plastics
from industrial waste; bioenergy/fuel from industrial waste; Biosensors/Biomarkers; Biodiversity
conservation of endangered/threatened/plant and animal species and Mitigation technology for
climate change. The R&D programmes addressed development of technology packages, tools,
techniques and processes for use by public and private sectors. Already few technologies packages
are available and few of them transferred to users.
The department has supported a special programme under Centres of Excellence for design
and development of anti-virals for Hepatitis ‘C’, vaccines research platform for HIV/AIDS, invitro
screening laboratories for microbicidal compounds. Proposals are also approved for antiviral drug
discovery programme and development of genome based diagnostics methods as a part of the
activities in the new institutions of DBT to be established in the Eleventh plan.
Comments
The Committee notes the efforts undertaken by the Department and is of the
opinion that sustained efforts are required to use technology as a tool to ensure
development in agriculture and its widespread use by farmers at the ground level.
RECOMMENDATION (PARA 5.3)
The Committee would also like the Department to focus and channelize its R&D activities
on programmes for using algae and jatropha as a source of biodiesel and producing ethanol from
cellulose because the sources of fossil fuel are depleting fast but yet constitute the major source
of energy. This should be done in a targeted manner so as to make early breakthroughs.
Action Taken by the Government
The Department of Biotechnology is supporting a major programme on Energy Bioscience
focusing on Biodiesel and Bioethanol from varied feed stocks. Quality planting material of Jatropha
from more than 2,500 accessions has been collected from across the country and characterized at
chemical and molecular level. The superior accessions have been multiplied and field planted over
and area of nearly 800 hectares for multi-location trials at 10 locations across the country. A
coordinated programme is also being supported on Bioethanol production from cellulosic biomass.
Leads have been obtained at the laboratory level, for agriculture and forestry waste. Recombinant
microorganisms for efficient ethanol recovery have been identified, the technology is now being
scaled up. In case of Algae feedstock for biofuel projects have been shortlisted for screening and
collection of strains from across the country, genetic improvement of strains for desired lipid levels
and developing photobioreactor systems for efficient production of the superior strains on mass
scale.
Comments
The Committee feels that research and development activities on finding a substitute
for fossil fuel has become the need of the hour, in view of the outgo of huge amounts of
foreign exchange for purchase of fossil fuels from abroad and, therefore, Committee is of
the opinion that research in this field should be accorded top priority.

5
RECOMMENDATION (PARA 6.4)
The Committee would like the Department to disseminate proven and field tested
technologies to help the rural population in their skill development, employment and income
generation in the field of agriculture, sericulture, etc. This has a potential not only to provide self-
employment and raise farm incomes but also to check migration to the cities, which are already
under stress. Self Help Groups along with other civil society groups need to be roped in big way
to make such programmes reach tribal, women and other weaker section of the society.
Action Taken by the Government
As on May 2008, the department has supported 2800 projects under progarmmes for
promoting biotechnology applications for the benefit of women, SC/ST and rural population. These
projects have been implemented benefiting about 2.5 lakhs people, which are implemented through
Krishi Vigyan Kendras, NGOs, and self help groups with technical support from central/states R&D
institutes, universities/colleges and research foundations. Progrmmes include projects for self
employment, additional income generation and improving health and agriculture practices. Efforts
are also being made to launch major programmes having impact at national level through
appropriate linkages with other ministries and their programmes.
Comments
The Committee hopes that projects promoting bio-technology applications for the
benefit of the rural masses should be popularized through proper coordination with various
State Governments, so as to ensure its widespread use.
RECOMMENDATION (PARA 7.2)
The Committee has been informed that the country produces lesser number of PhDs, in
comparison to other developing countries like Brazil and China except in engineering. This has
grave implications for Scientific Research in future. The Committee recommends that this situation
be rectified so as to create a good research base in the country and that the Department must play
a pro-active role in this regard. The number of PhDs is bound to less unless and until students
are initiated in the subject at a young age. The Department should evolve a suitable long-term
mechanism for the purpose. But the Committee feels that this would not be possible as the
allocation under this programme is Rs.30 crores as against Rs.70 crores proposed. The Committee
is of the opinion that adequate resources should be earmarked for Human Resource Development.
Action Taken by the Government
In so far, as the department is concerned within its mandate, 4 majors progarmmes/
strategies have been developed for addressing the issue of producing more number of quality PhDs
in Life Sciences:
(i) About 200 Ph.D. fellowships are supported through biotechnology entrance tests on
annual basis. The budgetary requirements are met out of the scheme “Human
Resource Development”. Keeping view of the suggestions of the committee, the
budgetary requirements will be revised at RE stage based on expenditure;
(ii) Under a separate scheme “Upgradation /reengineering of Universities”, selected 2-3
universities per year will be provided with adequate budget for increasing number of
PhD scholars/fellowships alongwith expenditure support for additional faculty and
research infrastructure of globally competitive nature. This programme is expected to
generate about 1000 Ph.Ds;

6
(iii) Under another separate scheme “Reentry Fellowships for early, medium and senior
career scientists of India”, resident in foreign countries shall be provided with salary,
infrastructure and laboratory support for taking up positions in universities/institutions
in India. In this context, a joint programme with WELCOME trust, UK and DBT has
been approved recently for a period of 5 years. This programme is also expected to
widen the research base; and
(iv) Under each of the 8 new institutions to be established/implemented by DBT in the
Eleventh plan, an estimated number of 800 Ph.D. fellowships will be made available.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and reiterates that a long term mechanism should
be evolved by the department to generate an interest towards science, right from the school
level.
RECOMMENDATION (PARA 8.2)
The Committee is of the opinion that financial and technical support should be given to
individual innovators as good innovations many a times come from the unorganized sector. The
Committee is of the opinion that the Department should do all needful in spreading the culture of
knowledge based entrepreneurship.
Action Taken by the Government
The department would like to clarify that the biotechnology entrepreneurship is research
intensive and requires minimum expertise in subjects related to biological sciences. However,
programmes under the scheme “Biotechnology based programme for societal Development”
addresses selective needs of entrepreneurship development in unorganized sector among women,
SC/ST population and rural areas. The suggestions of the committee shall be implemented through
this programme in a more focused manner. In the formal/organized sector, the department has
already launched two major programmes namely (a) Innovative Young Biotechologist Awards’ for
young researchers below the age of 35 years for research in frontier areas, about 25 awards
already been given as on date; (b) A programme Young Entrepreneurs Scheme (YES) in
collaboration with Government of UK was implemented by the department as one time activity. The
programme aims to encourage biotechnology entrepreneurship in young post-graduate and doctoral
students by exposing them to issues involved in commercialization of bio-science. A one-time team
of 5 members each present a commercial idea in the realm of biotechnology have been successfully
selected. Based on the suggestions of the committee, a similar programme is evolved for
implementation by the department from 2008-09 onwards.
Comments
The Committee hopes that the Department through its various programmes is able
to generate entrepreneurship development especially in the rural areas.
RECOMMENDATION (PARA 9.2)
The Committee welcomes the idea of spreading the scheme to Universities by setting up of
university-incubators in selected universities based on previous performances in life sciences. This
will not only bring the universities in the ambit of professional research but also mobilize contract
assignments from small and medium industries and promote academia-industry interaction thus
helping universities to get more exposure for good research.

7
Action Taken by the Government
As a follow up, the department has initiated proposals for establishment of university-
Industry incubators at University of Hyderabad, Hyderabad and University of Agricultural Sciences,
Bangalore through brain storming workshop involving stakeholders. Techno-economic feasibility
reports have been commissioned for the purpose.
Comments
The Committee is of the opinion that more number of universities across the country
require high quality scientific equipments for research purposes and the department with its
resources can play a pivotal role in this regard.
RECOMMENDATION (PARA 10.2)
The Committee desires that the Centre should continue its research work in the areas of
Hepatitis, Malaria, recombinant gene product, plant molecular biology, plant resistance, plant
transformation, etc., which help for the development of Biotechnology in our country. The
Committee is of the opinion that there is a lot to learn from the developed counties in the field
of genetic engineering to address the health needs of our country. The Institute can play a pivotal
role in coordinating scientific and technological exchanges with the west so as to obtain vital inputs
for our health research.
Action Taken by the Government
As suggested by the committee, measures have been initiated for continuous support to
research work carried out by International Centure for Genetic Engineering and Biotechnolgy
(ICGEB) with international and national linkages. Proposal for acquisition of new powerful tool to
identify new drug targets in national drug development programmes has been approved.
Comments
The Committee feels that the Department should coordinate with the foreign scientific
institutions on a regular basis so as to garner knowledge gained by them and ensure faster
development of biotechnology in the country.
RECOMMENDATION (PARA 11.2)
The Committee is of the opinion that the Department should take serious and sincere steps
to make project/schemes for benefit of North Eastern Region and Sikkim successful by not just
allocating funds but also creating capacity to absorb these funds. The Committee feels that this
scheme should be seen as an opportunity to involve local communities and provide them
employment.
Action Taken by the Government
As a follow up, the department has established a special cell for North Eastern Areas to
implement targeted programmes. The cell with adequate technical and supporting staff would assist
these areas generation of projects of viable nature benefitting in capacity building and monitoring
for timely implementation of projects both in terms of technical and financial goals. The projects
shall implement with overall goal of improving quality life sciences education, research and benefit
to local communities besides employment generation and entrepreneurship development.

8
Comments
The Committee is of the opinion that the North-Eastern region of the country
requires special support as regards development in scientific field and all out efforts are
required to make the schemes a complete success, which would result in economic
development of the region.
RECOMMENDATION (PARA 12.2)
The Committee has been informed that while 7000 patents were filed globally, there were
only two patents from India. The reason being lacunae in our institutional design and in our
strategy for getting cutting-edge scientists. The Committee emphasized the need to improve the
incentive structure so as to attract good scientists and make efforts for the same. The Committee
is of the view that post-doctoral fellowships are very low and need to be increased to retain our
scientists in the country.
Action Taken by the Government
Keeping in view of the suggestions of the committee, adequate attention has been paid for
technology management in all the new institutions and ongoing institutions as well as major projects
funded. A programme for reentry fellowships has been launched to be implemented by the
department in collaboration with WELCOME Trust, UK for attracting young Indian scientist from
abroad to take up position in Indian Institutions/Universities in the cutting edge areas of research.
The matter of increasing of post doctoral has been taken up by the department with the Ministry
of Finance. Accordingly, the fellowships have been increased from Rs.11000/- (1st year)—
Rs.12000/- (3rd year onwards) to Rs.l6000/- and Rs.18000/- respectively w.e.f. 01.04.2007.
Comments
The Committee appreciates the increase in the amount of Post Doctoral Fellowships and
feels that this is a step in the right direction for providing incentive to the young scientist.
RECOMMENDATION (PARA 12.3)
The Committee is further of the view that in a dynamic and competitive environment, quick
decision-making is the key to success. Owing to involvement of several ministries in decision-
making process, initiation and implementation of schemes gets considerably slowed down in our
country. It is, therefore, required that a better coordination at different levels of decision-making
is established so that opportunities are not lost due to undue delays.
Action Taken by the Government
Recognizing the need for coordination for implementation of national biotechnology
development strategy formulated by the department as well as for the programmes for the Eleventh
Plan, the department has constituted an inter-ministerial committee involving all the concerned
ministries and departments. The first meeting of the committee was also held in May 2008. This
step will ensure prompt coordination and decision making for implementation of schemes.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and reiterates that without proper coordination
amongst the various ministries which are involved in the decision making process, faster
implementation of the schemes will not be possible.
