PREFACE
I, the Chairman of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Science and
Technology, Environment and Forests, having been authorised by the Committee to present the
Report on its behalf, present this One Hundred and Ninety-seventh Report on the Action Taken by
the Department of Scientific and Industrial Research on the recommendations contained in the One
Hundred and Eighth-sixth Report of the Committee on Demands for Grants (2008-09) of the
Department of Scientific and Industrial Research.
2. The Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Department of Scientific
and Industrial Research on the recommendations contained in the One Hundred and Eighty-sixth
Report of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Science and Technology,
Environment and Forests on the Demands for Grants (2008-09) of the Department of Scientific and
Industrial Research which was presented to the Rajya Sabha on 29th April, 2008.
3. There were Nineteen recommendations contained in the One Hundred and Eighty-sixth Report
of the Committee. Action Taken Notes on the recommendations of the Committee were received
from the Department on 31st July, 2008.
4. In the meeting held on 13th October, 2008 the Committee considered the draft Action Taken
Report and adopted the same.
DR. V . MAITREYAN
N
EW D ELHI; Chairman,
October 13, 2008 Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on
Science and Technology, Environment and Forests

1
REPORT
The Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Department of Scientific
and Industrial Research on the recommendations contained in the One Hundred and Eighty-sixth
Report of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Science and Technology,
Environment and Forests on the Demands for Grants (2008-09) of the Department of
Scientific and Industrial Research, which was presented to both the Houses of Parliament on
29th April, 2008. There were Nineteen recommendations in the One Hundred Eighty-sixth Report
of the Committee. Action Taken Notes on the recommendations of the Committee were received
from the Department on 31st July, 2008.
The Committee’s recommendations, action taken thereon and further comments of the
Committee on the Action Taken by the Department of Scientific and Industrial Research are set out
in the succeeding paragraphs:
RECOMMENDATION (PARA 2.3)
The Committee expresses serious concern over the token hike in the allocation for the
Department. It feels that this hike is basically no hike if the growth rate of 9 per cent and the
inflation of 5 per cent is taken into consideration. It only shows the amount of importance that
the Government today attaches to scientific organization like DSIR. The Committee is of the
opinion that the axe of routine cut should not fall on scientific departments as it would adversely
affect research and development which is vital for the development of the nation. The Committee,
therefore, recommends that the well thought out projected demand of scientific department should
be honoured and accepted by the Planning Commission, more so when the department has the
capacity and the readiness to absorb additional funds.
Action Taken by the Government
The Department takes note of Committee’s recommendation. The Department indeed has the
capacity to absorb more funds and is accordingly approaching Planning Commission, again, to hike
plan allocation so as to enable the Department to take up more of R&D projects.
Comments
The Committee feels that the future of the country depends upon its technological
prowess and the research and development projects of the Department play an
important role in this regard. Any unjustified decrease in funds allocation would slow
the country’s progress. Hence the Committee reiterates that the Department should pursue
its demand for higher allocation with the Planning Commission more vigorously at R.E.
stage.
RECOMMENDATION (PARA 3.3)
The Committee is pleased to know that a mechanism to monitor and review the ongoing
schemes has been put in place by the Department. The Committee hopes that the Department will
further strengthen this mechanism for effective implementation of its programmes.
Action Taken by the Government
The Department thankfully acknowledges the remarks of the Committee. The Department

2
will endeavour to put in place a transparent monitoring and review mechanism that will
enable it to implement its programmes as per the desired objectives and within the agreed time
frame.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.
RECOMMENDATION (PARA 4.4)
The Committee takes serious note of such laxity on the part of the Department in utilization
of funds and recommends that the Department should make full use of its Project Monitoring
Committee so that funds could be utilized substantially for the purpose intended and within the time
frame set for the same. The Committee also recommends that optimum utilization of enhanced
budgetary allocation this year should be made by the Department.
Action Taken by the Government
The Department shares the concern of the Committee regarding non-utilization of the funds
allocated to it last year. The Department shall strive earnestly for optimum utilization of funds
allocated to it during the current year.
Comments
The Committee hopes that the Department will endeavour to fully utilize the funds
through its project monitoring committees.
RECOMMENDATION (PARA 4.5)
The Committee is of the view that small and medium industrial units should be encouraged
to develop competitive technologies, as innovations are not necessarily dependent on huge
funding and many a times break-through comes from small and medium research units. What
is more required is the right guidance by the Department to researchers and their organizations
on commercial issues so that results of their efforts are not made use of by other market
predators.
Action Taken by the Government
The Department is in total agreement with the Committee’s view that small and medium
industrial units need to be supported for development of innovative technologies. For this reason,
the Department has initiated a programme aimed at small businesses viz. ‘Technology Development
and Demonstration Programme - Small Businesses’, during the Eleventh plan period.
Comments
The Committee hopes that the ‘Technology Development and Demonstration
Programme Small Businesses’ will be a success during the Eleventh Plan period and provide
the required impetus to the small and medium industrial units.
RECOMMENDATION (PARA 5.3)
National Research Development Corporation (NRDC)
The budgetary allocations for 2008-09 for this programme is Rs.10 crores as

3
against Rs.8.00 crores during the year 2007-08. The Committee feels that this is a very useful
and important programme of the Department which encourages meritorious inventions
having commercial potential by giving awards, provide technical and financial assistance for
filing patents in India and abroad for protecting intellectual property and also helps in
dissemination of information on rural technologies and promotion of entrepreneurship among
rural masses. The Committee is of the opinion that this programme needs to be strengthened
and intensified. The Department should think in terms of providing more funds for this
programme.
Action Taken by the Government
The Department thankfully acknowledges the remarks of the Committee. NRDC, a Public
Sector Undertaking (PSU) of the Department, has been awarding meritorious inventions to
encourage inventors and keep their innovative spirit alive. During 2007-08, NRDC awarded
five meritorious inventions and also gave away a WIPO Gold Medal for best invention. During
2008-09, NRDC has invited applications from inventors in three categories, viz. innovation award
of the year, societal innovation award and budding innovators award. The department would
support NRDC in strengthening and intensifying this programme.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and recommends that besides National Research
Development Corporation, the other units of the Department should also initiate schemes
to provide encouragement through awards to meritorious inventions.
RECOMMENDATION (PARA 5.4)
The Committee was informed that there is a rural show case centre of the Department
which helps in disseminating appropriate rural technology to the rural masses. The Committee is
of the view that rural showcasing of scientific achievements is of immense importance, as progress
in scientific research should be shared with the rural population and through an interactive process
local knowledge should be harnessed in the larger interest. The Committee would like the
Department to have more such rural show case centres to inculcate scientific temper among the
masses.
Action Taken by the Government
NRDC has set up a network of Rural Technology Demonstration-cum-T raining (R TDT)
Centres in association with NGOs for dissemination of appropriate rural technologies to the rural
masses and inculcating scientific temper among them. During the last year, NRDC established a
‘carpet weaving centre’ in Nagaland. NRDC has identified three sectors, viz. sericulture, dairy and
coir for technological interventions so as to assist the entrepreneurs/units in these clusters to
optimize production. As advised by the Committee, the Department would encourage NRDC to
establish a larger number of rural showcase and RTDT Centres to inculcate scientific temper
among masses.
Advanced Materials and Processes Research Institute (AMPRI), a constituent laboratory of
CSIR, has set up a ‘Rural Gallery’ in its campus at Bhopal. The gallery showcases products,
related to rural folks, developed by various CSIR laboratories. AMPRI is also planning to set-up
a Mobile Rural Gallery for efficient dissemination of S&T interventions in products and processes
for masses.

4
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and hopes that the Department would finalize a time
bound plan and set up RTDT centres to share the knowledge gained in the laboratories with
the rural masses.
RECOMMENDATION (PARA 5.9)
Central Electronics Ltd. (CEL)
The Committee has been informed that the Department is striving to develop photovoltaic
cells through which solar energy could be used on a large scale. For this purpose it is working
on nano-material which has high absorption capacity per unit area and can go a long way in
making storage devices small and portable. The Committee observes that the Department should
explore the possibilities of exploiting more and more solar energy and in the long run it should aim
at replacing the conventional source of energy with solar energy. To achieve this objective it should
look for technologies like nano-technology to improve storage and conversion of solar energy into
usable energy sources. The Committee is of the opinion that the Department should make all out
efforts in this direction more so because conventional source of energy are regarded as adding to
the environmental pollution and global warming
Action Taken by the  Government
Presently, CEL is manufacturing crystalline silicon solar cells and modules in a plant of
10 MWp capacity. Besides crystalline silicon solar cells, thin film and nano technology based solar
cells with higher conversion efficiency are also available in the world market, although these have
a market share of just 15%. CEL, also plans to start R&D work for development of thin film dye-
synthesized/organic solar cells in association with research institutions.
The Department shares the concern of the Committee that the conventional sources of
energy are adding to environmental pollution and global warming and as advised by the Committee
would support CEL’s endeavours to develop and manufacture thin film/nano technology based solar
cells.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and recommends that the research and development
work in manufacturing cheap solar photovoltaic cells should be accorded top priority,
so that solar power can be provided to the poor sections of the society at an affordable
cost.
RECOMMENDATION (PARA 5.9.1)
The Committee has also been informed that it is possible to run some water pumping sets
on solar energy. The Committee is of the view that such possibilities should be fully explored as
they have a great potential to solve irrigation problems and raise farm incomes particularly in the
rural areas where there is lack of electricity
Action Taken by the Government
CEL has so far supplied more than 2000 solar water pumping systems to various state nodal
agencies under Programmes of Ministry of New and Renewable Energy and Drinking Water
Mission Programme of Department of Rural Development. It will continue to supply more such
systems in rural areas for the purpose of irrigation.

5
Comments
The Committee feels that solar water pumping systems have a great potential,
keeping in view that India is basically an agrarian economy and, therefore, recommends
more such pumps may be supplied to the farmers across the country at subsidized
prices.
RECOMMENDATION (PARA 10.3)
Solar power operated reverse osmosis desalination unit
The Committee is of the opinion that the Department in co-ordination with other
departments and agencies should also explore possibilities of converting saline water to drinking
water while working on technologies to convert saline water to irrigation water at low cost. The
Committee also feels that the network of such plan should be expanded so that more and more
people could be benefited by it.
Action Taken by the Government
CSIR, along with Department of Atomic Energy is formulating a project proposal at a cost
of Rs.742.00 crore (Rs.140.00 crore CSIR’s component and 602.00 crore DAE component). This
is to provide safe drinking water to a significant number of habitations and house holds in rural
areas through installation of desalination and water purification systems.
A lot of work has already been done in development of desalination plants using
various power sources including solar and even draught animals. The Department is conscious
of the enormity of the requirement to supply safe drinking water to maximum possible number
of persons.
Comments
The Committee is of the opinion that sustained efforts are required for the
development and setting up of the desalinization plants across the country. The Committee
further urges that a time frame be worked out for implementation of the scheme.
RECOMMENDATION (PARA 11.6)
Council of Scientific and Industrial Research
The Committee is aware that CSIR is involved in developing cost effective generic drugs
and standardization of Herbal and Ayurvedic drugs. It is also engaged in development of
commercially viable technologies for life saving drugs such as anti virals, anti cancer, anti bacterial,
cardio-vascular, etc. It is also designing and developing instrumentation for diagnostics
therapeutics and life supporting system among others. But the fact remains that diseases like
malaria, polio, diabetes, tuberculosis, cancer, etc. are still rampant in the country and are taking
a heavy toll. Treatment of some of these diseases are still beyond the reach of common man. The
benefit of scientific research is yet to percolate down to the society. The Committee, therefore,
recommends that the department should seriously make an introspection and try to address these
issues on priority basis in a time bound manner.
Action Taken by the Government
The recommendation of the Committee is appreciated. V arious institutes of CSIR, like
CDRI, IMTECH, IIM, IGIB, IICT etc. are involved in the process of drug discovery and

6
development. So far, CSIR has been successful in developing 12 out of 17 drugs which have been
developed post independence within the country.
CSIR has initiated R&D programme on ‘New Development for parasitic diseases’,
development and commercialization of bioactive and traditional preparations etc. Under these
programmes expertise available within various laboratories of CSIR are networked and joint efforts
are being undertaken to discover and develop drugs for diseases like cancer, tuberculosis, malaria,
diabetes etc. A number of promising leads have been identified and are at various stages of drug
discovery and development process through these programmes.
CSIR has also formulated a programme for ‘Open Source Drug Discovery’, through which
development of drugs for tuberculosis is being taken up initially. The approach of this programme
is web-based and would involve scientists not only from CSIR but also experts from universities,
students, industry etc. within and outside India. It is presumed that this approach would be helpful
in reducing the cost of drug discovery and development process and ultimately help in making the
drugs available at a lower cost.
Comments
The Committee expresses its concern over the fact that the Department is yet to find
a complete solution to common man’s diseases viz. Malaria, Polio, Tuberculosis, etc., though
a lot of funds and effort has been invested for the purpose. The Committee therefore,
recommends that research and development efforts should be intensified to find medication
for these diseases at the earliest.
RECOMMENDATION (PARA 11.7)
The Committee is also aware that the department is engaged in developing technology and
know-how for environment friendly conversion and utilization of bio mass to fuels. The Committee
has been informed that during 2008-09 the Department has targeted to make preliminary
experiments on bio fuels and has developed heterogeneous catalyst for bio diesel production,
process for production of bio ethanol from cellulose and starch. The Committee feels that fossil
fuel, besides being costly, is a major source of pollution in the environment. There is an urgent
need to seek an economically viable and environment friendly alternative. The Committee, therefore,
recommends that the tempo of research and development should be accelerated so that the country
could reap the benefits at the earliest. The Committee, however, desires that while developing bio
fuels, care should be taken not to use edible cereals as it may affect the poor adversely.
Action Taken by the Government
CSIR has been executing projects, during Eleventh Plan, for development of environment-
friendly technology for conversion and utilization of bio-mass to fuels. None of the activity utilizes
edible cereals as a source of bio-fuel.
Comments
In view of the shortage of biofuel in the country and huge outgo of financial
resources due to their import, the Committee reiterates that Research and Development on
commercially viable biofuel should be given top priority.
RECOMMENDATION (PARA 11.8)
The phenomena of Global warming and climate change are emerging as one of the greatest

7
and most formidable challenges of the 21st century which are stated to have the potential of
pushing the world to the brink of catastrophe. Adaptation and mitigation are the two possible ways
and means identified to counter their effects. But these are not so easy solutions as they appear
to be. Science has to play a pivotal role in this direction. Department of Scientific and Industrial
Research with its vast network of multi disciplinary laboratories and huge resource of competent
and expert man power has to take a lead role in galvanizing and dovetailing its activities and
resources to find viable solutions to provide relief to the nation and the world from this impending
calamity. It can address scientific issues relevant to atmosphere, geosphere, hydrosphere as well
as biosphere. It can assume the responsibility of standardizing all measurement of global change
with international traceability. The Committee is happy to note that CSIR is contemplating to initiate
a mega R&D programme on climate change covering various dimensions such as assessment,
adaptation, mitigation, alternate energy sources, etc. Since this has to be addressed on an urgent
and immediate basis, the Committee is of the opinion that the Department should start working on
this at the earliest without losing any time, in a time bound manner, efficacy of which may be
reviewed annually. Progress made in this regard may be brought before the public in the form of
a white paper or in any form the Department deems appropriate so that people could not only feel
assured but also come to know how real and formidable is the threat posed by global warming
and climate change. The Committee also feels that separate budgetary provisions for this purpose
could be made.
Action Taken by the Government
The recommendation of the Committee is well taken. CSIR has taken deep cognizance of
the PM’s National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC) and is in the process of formulating
and restructuring programmes in tune with the expectations of NAPCC. Few recent initiatives
launched are “Sequestration of atmospheric CO
2 by Iron-fertilization”, “Assessment and
management of environmental pollutants”, “Eco-restoration and cleanup of contaminated sites”,
“Mapping of marine biodiversity along the Indian Coast” etc. with requisite budgetary support. The
outcome of these projects shall be appropriately disseminated. In order to meet above objective, all
the proposals required for patenting are thoroughly scrutinized and necessary suggestions are made
to laboratories to provide/generate required data for the above said purposes. Similarly, special
emphasis has also been laid on the projects arising out of public-private partnership and protection
of IP generated from such coordinated efforts.
Comments
The Committee appreciates the initiation of various projects by the department and
hopes that the outcome of these projects would result in formulation of plans on an urgent
basis to mitigate the problem of climate change.
RECOMMENDATION (PARA 12.5)
National Laboratories
The Committee feels that the R&D activities can be undertaken only in laboratories and
unless we have a network of rich and sophisticated labs we can not make advancement in the field
of science. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the budgetary demands of the Department
for such crucial programme needs to be fully met and they should be provided enhanced funds
at RE stage in case, they demand. The Committee has taken note that the Department could initiate
only 76 out of 94 priority projects under the National Laboratories Scheme, during 2007-08. The
Committee would have been happy if all the priority projects could have been initiated during the
period they were intended.

8
Action Taken by the Government
CSIR is taking all efforts to initiate all of its priority-l projects. In addition to 76
priority-l projects as reported earlier, eight more project have been initiated. Rest of the projects
are in the final stage of formulation. More funds needed to meet the project requirement.
Comments
The Committee hopes that all the Priority projects are initiated as per schedule and
the issue of additional funds requirement should be emphatically taken up with the
Planning Commission at the R.E. stage as recommended by the Committee earlier.
RECOMMENDATION (PARA 12.6)
The Committee has been informed that some of the CSIR laboratories like those in Kolkata
and Hyderabad are facing difficulty in expansion as they are located in the heart of the city with
very little space. The Committee is of the opinion that these premier organizations need new
buildings for better functioning. The Committee suggests that the Department may take up the
matter with the concerned State Governments to acquire land for the said purpose.
Action Taken by the Government
Kolkata:  Department, through its constituent laboratory Central Glass and Ceramic
Research Institute, Kolkata has approached Government of West Bengal for allotment of land in
Baruipur, Kolkata. Response from Government of West Bengal is awaited.
Hyderabad: On request of the Department (through Centre for Cellular and Molecular
Biology, Hyderabad), Government of Hyderabad has given ‘in-principle’ approval for allocation of
150 acres of land in the Phase-III, Biotech Park, Karkapatla, free of cost  for setting up a world
class dedicated Institute of Translational Research in Hyderabad. However due to certain reasons
such as lack of medical hospitals, medical schools, land is far away from CCMB etc. Department
approached Government of A.P. to consider allocating alternate land. On the suggestion of
Government of A.P., Department approached Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers, for allocating
150 acres of land in IDPL campus at Balanagar. IDPL has already given around 142 acres of land
to NIPER in that campus. Department is yet to receive response from the Ministry of Chemicals
and Fertilizers.
Comments
The Committee hopes that the issue of allotment of land is persued by the
Department with various agencies involved to ensure expansion of its institutes at the
earliest.
RECOMMENDATION (PARA 13.3 AND 13.4)
Research Schemes, Scholarship and Fellowships
The Committee welcomes the enhancement in allocations for Research Schemes,
Scholarships and Fellowships. It also welcomes the fact that in the Eleventh Plan, emphasis is
being laid on promotion of R&D in Basic Sciences, Engineering Sciences and Inter-disciplinary
areas. It is of the opinion that paradigmatic breakthrough in science can be possible only if there
is progress in basic sciences which ultimately get translated to state-of-art technologies.

9
Human Resource Development is buzzword today in every sector of economy as it is of
paramount importance in the Nation building process and creating a knowledge society. But the
shortage of qualified, competent and dedicated manpower in the field of science is being felt not
only in India but the world over. This shortfall is such which cannot be bridged overnight. To
catch young students, nurture, groom and develop them into budding scientists, it is imperative that
a concerted and coordinated strategy is made on a long-term basis. Since CSIR has vast array of
labs and is one of the biggest public sector employer of scientists, it has to actively play a major
role in this effort. Merely by awarding some scholarships or awards, this daunting task is not going
to be accomplished. The committee, therefore, recommends that DSIR must come out with some
concrete proposals to trap, harness and retain human resource in the field of science by earmarking
sufficient fund for the purpose.
Action Taken by the Government
During Eleventh Plan, a long-term, comprehensive ‘Human Resource Development Scheme’
has been proposed to identify and nurture budding young scientific talent in the area of basic
‘science, engineering and inter-disciplinary science and to encourage them to take up science as
a career by way of granting necessary incentives in the form of fellowships. This process would
naturally entail reversing the present flow of talent away from science.
Comments
The Committee hopes that the ‘Human Resource Development Scheme’ would not
remain a scheme merely on paper, but would be implemented in letter and spirit to bridge
the acute shortfall in the requirement of scientific manpower.
RECOMMENDATION (PARA 14.3)
Intellectual Property and Technology Management
The Committee feels that there is still a lot to be done to improve awareness about patents
in the country, especially among the scientist and other innovators so that the valuable intellectual
property earned by them is commercially protected. It is of the opinion that the Department should
make more efforts to increase the reach of such awareness programmes.
Action Taken by the Government
The suggestion of the Committee is well taken and the Department is regularly disseminating
through training programmes/Workshops the importance and need of IPR in our R&D programmes.
Some of the initiatives taken are:
• Training of interns and women scientists
During 2004-2008, 12 research interns/women scientists have been trained by CSIR in the
area of IP Management for a period of 1 and 2 years, under the scheme ‘CSIR Diamond
Jubilee Research Intern Awards’, and TIF AC-DST Scheme for the ‘women Scientist
Scholarship’. Many of these Interns/Women scientists now have been recruited by attorney
firms and Government departments.
• CSIR Diamond Jubilee Invention Award for School Children (CDJIA)
In order to enhance creativity and also to improve awareness of IP amongst school
children, CSIR announced 7th CSIR Diamond Jubilee Invention Award for School Children-

10
2008 on 26 April, WORLD IN TELLECTUAL PROPERTY DA Y . During the last six years,
2221 proposals have been received for this competition from school children from various
parts of the country and 41 inventions were selected for various prizes by a High Level A
ward Committee.
• Training programmes on IP
Human Resource Development Centre (HRDC), CSIR, Ghaziabad, organized a number of
training programmes on IP during the year 2007. The programmes were attended not only
by scientists from various CSIR labs/other R&D institutes/organizations but also from
corporate sector,
Comments
The Committee is of the opinion that more number of training programmes/
workshops should be conducted at various universities/colleges/schools, to educate the
scientist about patents.
RECOMMENDATION (PARA 15.4)
New Millennium India Technology Leadership Initiative
The Committee is pleased to learn that ‘industries which partnered NMITLI projects have
been highly benefited not only in terms of the objectives and achievements in the projects wherein
they participated but also in terms of other associated gains such as high quality technical inputs’.
It is also heartening to know that during the Tenth Plan the New Millennium Indian Technology
Leadership Initiative (NMITLI) has created a brand image and is viewed today as a benchmark of
Public-Private Partnership (PPP) schemes which is being emulated by various other Government
Departments. The Committee is of the view that the public-private partnership is the kind of
research model that can successfully work in today’s world where commercial viability of research
and its self-sustaining nature is as important as the research itself.
Action Taken by the Government
The Department is thankful for appreciation.
Comments
The Committee hopes that NMITLI projects would be taken up with the
various governments in the right earnest, so that all the States may benefit by this
programme.
RECOMMENDATION (PARA 17.2)
The Committee, in view of the increased responsibilities and activities of the Department,
supports the rise in the allocation for ‘Other Scientific Research’ and hopes the Department would
be able to meet its commitments.
Action Taken by the Government
The Department is thankful for the Committee’s support for rise in allocation for ‘Other
Scientific Research’.

11
Comments
The Committee hopes that the department would be able to satisfy the aspirations
of the country as regards growth of scientific research and development, providing scientific
manpower and other associated responsibilities.

PREFACE
I, the Chairman of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Science and
Technology, Environment and Forests, having been authorised by the Committee to present the
Report on its behalf, present this One Hundred and Ninety-eighth Report on the Action Taken by
the Department of Atomic Energy on the recommendations contained in the One Hundred and
Ninety-first Report of the Committee on Demands for Grants (2008-09) of the Department of
Atomic Energy.
2. The Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Department of Atomic
Energy on the recommendations contained in the One Hundred and Ninety-first Report of the
Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Science and Technology, Environment and
Forests on the Demands for Grants (2008-09) of the Department of Atomic Energy which was
presented to the Rajya Sabha on 29th April, 2008.
3. There were eighteen recommendations contained in the One Hundred and Ninety-first Report
of the Committee. Action Taken Notes on the recommendations of the Committee were received
from the Department on 22nd July, 2008.
4. In the meeting held on 13th October, 2008 the Committee considered the draft Action Taken
Report and adopted the same.
DR. V . MAITREYAN
N
EW D ELHI; Chairman,
October 13, 2008 Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on
Science and Technology, Environment and Forests.

1
REPORT
The report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Department of Atomic
Energy (DAE) on the recommendations contained in the one hundred and Ninety-first Report of the
Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Science and Technology, Environment and
Forests on the Demands for Grants (2008-09) of the Department of Atomic Energy, which was
presented to both the Houses of Parliament on 29th April, 2008. There were eighteen
recommendations in the One Hundred Ninety-first Report of the Committee. Action Taken notes on
the recommendations of the Committee were received from the Department on 22nd July, 2008.
Recommendation (Para 4.3. and 4.4)
The Committee, however, notes with serious concern the curtailment of funds under the Plan
schemes in Research and Development Sector for premier institutions like Bhabha Atomic Research
Centre, Indira Gandhi Centre for Atomic Research, Variable Energy Cyclotron Centre, Raja Ramanna
Centre for Advanced Technology, Atomic Minerals Directorate for Exploration and Research, Tata
Institute of Fundamental Research, Institute of Plasma Research, Saha Institute of Nuclear Physics,
Tata Memorial Centre, etc. The Power sector which is responsible for undertaking the ongoing
Nuclear Power Project under the Bharatiya Nabhikiya Vidyut Nigam Ltd. has also experienced a cut
in allocation. The Committee also notes the cuts in budgetary allocation under the non-plan schemes
which were intended for the operational budget in Industrial Sector in Heavy Water production,
Nuclear Fuel Complex, Board for Radiation and Isotope Technology, etc.
The Committee is of the opinion that curtailment of funds for premier Institutions engaged
in comprehensive research and development of frontline technologies, for harnessing nuclear energy
for the benefit of the society, would delay the endeavour of these institutions in achieving their
goals. The Committee fails to understand as to how the Department will manage to achieve its
targets, in the field of Atomic Energy, whi ch is highly capital intensive with such meager budgetary
allocations. The Committee hopes that in future the Planning Commission and the Ministry of
Finance would exercise utmost precaution before finalizing allocation for the Department.
Action Taken by the Government
The recommendations of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on
Science and Technology,- Environment & Forests has since been brought to the notice of Ministry
of Finance and to the Planning Commission for corrective steps so that utmost precaution is taken
by them before finalising the allocation for the Department in future.
Comments
The Committee hopes that the Department of Atomic Energy would henceforth put
forward its case for larger allocation of funds for its crucial programmes forcefully, so as
to ensure sufficient allocation of funds at the Budget Estimate stage itself.
Recommendation (Para No. 5.3)
The Committee desires that the existing monitoring mechanisms developed by the
Department to monitor and review the progress of the ongoing schemes/projects before
formulating/finalizing proposals for budgetary support should be effectively used to eliminate any
scope of shortage or surrender of funds at a later stage.

2
Action Taken by the Government
The existing monitoring mechanisms developed by the Department to monitor and review
the progress of the ongoing schemes/projects before formulating/finalising proposals for budgetary
support are being effectively used to eliminate the scope of shortage or surrenders of funds at a
later stage.
The recommendations of the Committee have been brought to the notice of all Heads of
Constituent Units/Autonomous Bodies and Public Sector Undertakings of the Department.
Comments
The Committee hopes that its recommendations will seriously be taken into account
in future also while formulating monitoring mechanisms.
Recommendation (Para 6.6)
The Committee feels that the reduction in the approved allocation vis-a-vis the proposed one
would somehow affect the programmes envisaged by the Department during the Eleventh Plan
some of which like upgradation and modernization are very crucial. The Committee is of the
opinion that the Department is in a better position to judge its requirements and hence surreptitious
or perfunctory reduction is untenable. Any compromise on major research programmes is not
acceptable to the Committee. This issue, therefore, needs to be seriously looked into by the
Government.
Action Taken by the Government
The concern expressed by the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on
Science and Technology, Environment and Forests has since been brought to the notice of Planning
Commission.
Comments
The Committee hopes that routine reduction in allocations would not be effected in
crucial programmes such as those conducted by the Department of Atomic Energy as it
affects the pace of the Research and Development.
Recommendation (Para 7.4)
The Committee is of the opinion that some precautionary measures should be taken by the
Department of Atomic Energy while irradiating food so that the possible health risks involved before
consumption of irradiated food could be effectively dealt with. In this connection a timebound
programme for evaluation of Radiological Safety, Microbiological Safety, Nutritional adequacy and
Toxicological Safety may be initiated since the irradiation of seed/food products is in a nascent
stage.
Action Taken by the Government
The concerns of possible health risks associated with the application of the technology have
already been addressed by several reputed institutions ar ound the world i ncluding Bhabha Atomic
Research Centre in studies devoted to testing wholesomeness and nutritional adequacy of irradiated
foods. These studies included testing of radiological, nutritional, chemical and microbiological safety
as well as feeding of animals and human volunteers. The results of these studies have been

3
thoroughly evaluated by Joint Expert Committees of the Food and Agricultural Organization, World
Health Organization and International Atomic Energy Agency, and no adverse effects have been
found. As a result, the Codex Alimentarius Commission and food and health authorities of several
nations including India have approved radiation processing of food.
At its own food irradiation facilities in V ashi and Lasalgaon, Department of Atomic Energy
is taking all the precautionary measures to ensure radiological safety, microbiological safety,
nutritional adequacy and toxicological safety of the irradiated food products. The dose employed
is specific for a technological purpose as approved by international regulatory agencies. It must
also be emphasized that irradiation is carried out on packaged food materials. Good laboratory
practices must be followed prior to and after packaging to ensure microbiological safety.
Department of Atomic Energy ensures these at its facilities and also carries out periodic testing of
samples for dose delivered as well as quality. The same requirements are insisted upon during and
after the transfer of knowhow to private sector irradiation facilities.
A detailed note providing therewith additional information regarding food irradiation is
annexed to this report (Annexure – A).
Comments
The Committee takes note of the reply and appreciates the steps taken by the
Department to eliminate possible health risks and ensure safety during food irradiation and
hopes that this technology would be encouraged and popularised in the country.
Recommendation (Para 8.2)
The Committee feels that diagnostic radiopharmaceuticals are an important constituent of the
various diagnostic tools used for the detection of life threatening diseases like cancer, thaleseemia,
tumors etc. and therefore desires that efforts should be made by the Department to produce
sufficient radiopharmaceuticals in the country itself and provide it to the hospitals at cheaper rates
so that the poor patients can avail of the facility.
Action Taken by the Government
Radiation Medicine Centre (RMC), Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC) operates the
Medical Cyclotron and produces F-18 FDG (18-F-Fluro Deoxy Glucose) for supply to various
Positron Emission Tomography (PET) Centres, in Mumbai and Pune through Board of Radiation
and Isotopes Technology, for use in diagnosis and follow-up of cancer. It will be setting up a
Central Radiopharmacy for 
99mTc-radiopharmaceuticals, in collaboration with Board of Radiation and
Isotopes Technology, for regular availability of 99mTcO4- to users in Mumbai. These supplies are
expected to be cheaper since indigenous generators from Board of Radiation and Isotopes
Technology will be used in place of imported 
99mTc generators. Radiation Medicine Centre will
continue to work synergistically with Bhabha Atomic Research Centre and Board of Radiation and
Isotopes Technology to develop and evaluate newer radiopharmaceuticals with 188-Rhenium and
68-Gallium.
Radiation Medicine Centre offers very low-cost (free for poor patients) Nuclear Medicine
scans using 
99mTc and 18F-radiopharmaceuticals to patients referred by other hospitals. It is
proposed to procure a state-of-art PET-CT scanner, and SPECT gamma camera during Eleventh
plan to augment these facilities. Radiation Medicine Centre is also conducting post-graduate diploma
courses for clinicians (two-year DRM) and technologists (one-year DMRIT) who are the backbone
of the practice and propagation of Nuclear Medicine in India.

4
Comments
The Committee appreciates the steps taken by the Radiation Medicine Centre, Bhaba
Atomic Research Centre for production of low cost and cheaper varieties of diagnostic radio
pharmaceuticals and hopes that efforts would be made to make available these medicines
at various hospitals throughout the country.
Recommendation (Para 9.2)
The Committee is of the opinion that cancer is one of the most prevalent diseases in India
afflicting the population across the country and the treatment for the disease is very costly.
Telemedicine is one of the tools of reducing the treatment cost, as it can provide specialised
treatment even at the backward and remote regions of the country. The Committee, therefore,
recommends that efforts should be made to spread the telemedicine network by connecting more
hospitals across the country with the Tata Memorial Hospital.
Action Taken by the Government
The concept of networking all the Regional Cancer Centres (RCCs) through telemedicine
originated from the cancer desk of the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. The project
TELEMEDICINE - CANTELMED was assigned to Tata Memorial Centre. The important aims and
objectives of the project is (1) to standardise and ensure practice of Evidence Based Medicine
(2) to improve access to cancer care and cancer initiatives in underserved areas and finally provide
hub and spoke services in the peripheral areas. (3) to reduce costs of cancer care delivery (4) to
export clinical expertise, increasing the availability of cutting edge cancer protocols and procedures
to all affiliate facilities (5) to be used as a training tool to promote continuing education and
development (6) to coordinate and monitor research for the DAE funded research protocols in the
RCCs and (7) to provide links to other networks and organisations.
The implementation was envisaged in phases to ensure gradual acceptance and integration
of the telemedicine services with the cancer care delivery system at the participating Institutions
as stated below:—
PHASE 1 (September 2003 - April 2004)
Tata Memorial Hospital, Mumbai was connected with Dr B Borooah Cancer Institute,
Guwahati and Dr B K Walavalkar Hospital Dervan, (rural outreach programme of Tata Memorial
Centre (TMCROP)), near Chiplun, Maharashtra.
PHASE 2 A ( May 2004 – December 2004)
Tata Memorial Hospital (TMH) established linkages with 14 other Centres,
including six in North East India and two overseas.
PHASE 2 B (Jan 2005 – Dec 2005)
Nine Hospitals including six Regional Cancer Centres were included in the network.
Phase III (2006)
Six Regional Cancer Centres were added in this Phase.
Post Phase III 2007-2008
Five centres have been added to the network.

The network has 31 centres connected consisting of 15 RCCs and 16 other Hospitals as
well as 2 overseas centres. The network has been used by remote nodes 31 for over 900
telemedicine and telepathology consultations. 17 Conferences and Continuing Medical Education
(CMEs) have been beamed out as teleeducation sessions and 10 international conferences have been

The telemedicine programme has been specially beneficial for the work up and treatment
planning for patients of BKW Hospital Dervan TMCROP for pre visit work up by the TMH
consultants. The patients taking advice at Hospitals in the North East have been spared a costly
and time consuming trip to Mumbai. Only 7 patients seen at remote sites were asked to come to

very high. Satisfaction with consultation is very high and most would repeat a follow up

Plans are in hand to expanding the reach of telemedicine through the Government of India
ONCONET Programme for Teleconsultations, medical education and also for connecting with
additional nodes on the ISRO network. It is also envisaged to increase patient education and

6
awareness for follow up from remote nodes. Further, it is indented to enhance the Value addition
through Regular CME by broadcasting weekly clinical meetings to the remote nodes and
Broadcasting lectures and demonstrations in Preventive Oncology and Early Detection, Nursing
Techniques, ICU care, Catheter Care, Infection Control etc.
All out effects are taken by the Department to spread the telemedicine network by
connecting more and more hospitals in the country.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply with satisfaction and urges that the work of
spreading the network is continued.
Recommendation (Para 10.4 and 10.5)
The Committee notes that, while allocations under some of the heads of the ‘Assistance to
Universities’ have been decreased, they have remained constant for most of the programmes like
public awareness and neighbourhood programme, exhibitions, symposia, etc. In some programmes
viz. fellowships, prospective research in funding, etc. insignificant increases have been effected.
The Committee is of the opinion that budgetary allocations under these heads are relatively meager,
keeping in view the fact that there is an urgent need to develop interest and awareness amongst
the masses and especially the younger generation towards the subject of Atomic Energy and to
dispel the negative impression of the public towards nuclear power. The Committee is of the
opinion that more funds should be allocated towards mass awareness programmes in the field of
nuclear science.
The Committee feels that the Department should concentrate on increasing its investments
significantly, in the field of research in nuclear science at University level, which would help in
inculcating interest towards nuclear science and attracting more students to this field. In this
direction the Committee recommends that a proactive system of funding should be initiated by the
department, which would focus towards bringing more and more universities across the country
under its coverage of grants.
Action Taken by the Government
The budget allocation towards Public Awareness and Neighbourhood Development
programmes referred to are pertaining to the allocation of expenditure towards this head only from
the DAE Secretariat (through its Public Awareness Division). In addition to this, its Public Sector
Undertakings (like Nuclear Power Corporation of India Limited, Uranium Corporation of India
Limited etc.), Industrial Organisations (like Board of Radiation and Isotopes Technology, Heavy
Water Board, Nuclear Fuel Complex etc.) and R&D organizations (like Atomic Minerals Directorate
for Exploration and Research, Bhabha Atomic Research Centre, Indira Gandhi Centre for Atomic
Research, Raja Ramanna Centre for Advanced Technology, Variable Energy Cyclotron Centre etc.)
are also carrying out such programmes in their respective neighbourhood. Both Nuclear Power
Corporation of India Limited and Uranium Corporation of India Limited conduct their own Public
Awareness and Neighbourhood development programmes in the villages surroundings their operating
facilities and also in the areas where they intend to set up new facilities. Thus, the overall
expenditure on Public Awareness and Neighbourhood Development is to the extent of requirement.
The Department of Atomic Energy (DAE) recognizes the need for funding the Indian
Universities and programmes are already in place to provide funding for carrying out R&D projects
on topics of interest to the mandate of the Department to leading universities, academic institutions
and recognized R&D labs in the country through the Board of Research in Nuclear Sciences

7
(BRNS). A typical distribution of BRNS funding for the past 10 years is shown in (Annexure-B).
The BRNS has not only helped several universities to establish excellent state-of-the-art labs/
facilities/centres enabling them to carry out high end research in the areas of nuclear science and
technology, but has also played a significant role in training human resources (both faculty and
students) in these areas.
In the past 2-3 years, there has been substantial increase in the efforts to enhance these
links further by proactive measures under BRNS by inviting senior faculty from local university /
colleges and NITs in the regional Theme Meetings for their larger participation in the DAE
programmes. A series of such meetings have already been conducted in the southern, Central and
northern region of the country which have yielded good return in terms of R&D projects,
registration of students for carrying out project work leading to post-graduate/doctoral degrees and
signing of several MoUs for tie-up with the DAE activities. Similar meetings are scheduled in other
parts of the country.
The DAE has also signed a MoU with Mumbai university for establishing a DAE-Mumbai
University-Centre of Excellence in Basic Sciences (CBS) in 2007 with a provision of total funding,
from BRNS, of Rs.52.00 crore during a period of five years. The Centre aims to offer integrated
MSc courses in physics, chemistry, life science, mathematics and computer sciences with major
emphasis on experimental science to the bright students in the country after (10+2) stage. While
the first batch in the Physics was started in 2007, batches in Chemistry and life sciences will be
commencing from Aug., 2008.
Department of Atomic Energy and University Institute of Chemical Technology, Mumbai
have entered into MoU for setting up the DAE-UICT Centre for Chemical Engineering Education
and Research in 2008 with an outlay of Rs.75.00 crore with the objectives such as: (1) to provide
Doctoral degrees to promising candidates with talent and aptitude for carrying out advanced
research and development activities in science and technology (2) to furnish a multidisciplinary,
flexible and innovative Ph.D research programme in Chemical Engineering with special emphasis
on, (a) Acquisition of proficiency in research, knowledge, data generation and analysis,
mathematical modeling, and management with sharpening skills in innovative experimental methods
and problem solving capabilities; (b) Creation of pool of young talented, dedicated and committed
individuals with passion and involvement in pursuing research and development as a career;
(c) inculcation of attitude, temper and outlook for developing social commitment as well as high
level of scientific ethics and integrity.
R&D units of Department of Atomic Energy such as Bhabha Atomic Research Centre,
Indira Gandhi Centre for Atomic Research, Raja Ramanna Centre for Advanced Technology, Atomic
Minerals Directorate for Exploration and Research etc. actively collaborate with local Universities
to motivate them to carry out research on topics of relevance to the Department of Atomic Energy.
Comments
The Committee appreciates the steps taken by the Department towards funding of
scientific institutions and various universities in carrying out research and development in
the field of Atomic Energy. The Committee also feels that the Department should initiate
such programmes at under graduate level to inculcate interest among the young science
students.
Recommendation (Para 11.5)
The Committee is of the opinion that the contribution to this sector is quite significant for
a developing economy like ours. There is a need to augment the existing programmes as it has a

8
direct bearing on the societal needs. Activities related to fuel fabrication, spent fuel recycling,
recovery of fissile and fertile materials, recovery of Uranium from secondary sources, etc. would
help the country to be less dependant on the external sources for pursuing our nuclear programme.
The Committee, therefore, recommends that the allocation of funds to this sector be augmented
adequately to meet the needs of activities being pursued by the Department.
Action Taken by the Government
The activities related to fuel fabrication, spent fuel recycling, recovery of fissile and fertile
materials, recovery of Uranium from secondary sources etc., have been augmented in Eleventh Plan
period. Towards this end Bhabha Atomic Research Centre has envisaged three major projects which
would help the country to be less dependant on the external sources for pursuing nuclear
programmes. (1) “Spent Fuel Recycle Project” with an outlay of Rs.970.00 crore; (2) “PUSHP AK”,
Tarapur, with an outlay of Rs.990.00 crore; (3) “Integrated Reprocessing and Waste Immobilisation
Plant”, Vizag, with an outlay of Rs.900.00 crore.
The main objective is to set up facilities to reprocess spent fuel discharged trom Pressurized
Heavy water Reactors (PHWR) and manage radioactive waste arising from the reprocessing
operations. As per the Indian nuclear power programme based on a closed fuel cycle, spent fuel
received from PHWRs is to be reprocessed to recover fissile and fertile materials and recycle the
same in the nuclear power plants.
Plutonium and Uranium will be separated from spent-fuel and purified to the specifications
for further handling and reuse. Plutonium is required as a fuel for the Fast Breeder Reactors
(FBRs) for producing power as well as for converting Thorium into fissile Uranium. The Plants
will reprocess spent fuels from PHWRs at the rated capacity of 300 tons/year and the separated
Plutonium will be made available for reuse in FBRs.
The PUSHPAK, at Tarapur will reprocess spent fuel from PHWRs of 220/500 MWe to
generate the input material for the second (Fast Breeder Reactors) of three stage power programme.
The liquid and waste generated during reprocessing operations will be treated and conditioned in WIP-
3B project to ensure safety to environment and general public on a long term basis.
The Integrated plant for fuel reprocessing and waste management with a capacity of 300
Te/yr of HM and a reprocessing plant with a capacity of 400 tonnes/year of heavy metals will be
set up for achieving recovery of fissile material, which in turn helps to meet the part demand of
fresh fuel for the nuclear reactors. It also includes treatment and conditioning of liquid, solid and
gaseous waste generated during the process operations. The interim storage of Vitrified Waste
Product canisters and solid alpha waste packages before disposal to underground geological
repository.
Similarly, Indira Gandhi Centre for Atomic Research is currently involved with technology
development of fuel fabrication and spent fuel reprocessing of Fast Reactors Fuels, besides
development of metanic fuels for future FBRs.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and reiterates that all such indigenous activities
which result in reducing dependence on external sources must be accorded top priority.
Recommendation (Para 12.2 and 12.3)
The Committee feels that both these technologies can prove to be boon for conservation
of nature and environment and for the society at large which is grappling with the problem of

9
disposal of sewage as well as solid waste generated in metropolitan cities and small towns. What
is required is the propagation and popularization of these technologies because their efficacy lies
in their use on a large scale. In view of the fact that environment protection is the need of the
hour as hazards of global warming and climate change are looming large, the urgency of such a
step becomes more prominent.
The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Department should take effective steps for
marketing these technologies, if possible by creating a special cell for the purpose, within Radiation
Technology Development Section of Bhabha Atomic Research Centre. The cell should interact with
the municipalities/corporations/State Governments/Ministry of Urban Development, Ministry of
Environment and Forests, etc. to demonstrate the merits of the technology.
Action Taken by the Government
Sludge Hygienization Research Irradiator (SHRI), in V adodara has provided valuable
experience regarding the design, operational parameters and irradiated sludge has been shown to be
useful as a fertilizer in agricultural practice. Efforts are on to popularize this technology by
constant interactions with large municipal bodies and Ministry of Urban Development.
The NISARGRUNA technology developed by Bhabha Atomic Research Centre offers a
comprehensive decentralized solution for handling the biodegradable waste materials. The process
combines aerobic and anaerobic degradation of the biodegradable waste materials and converts the
waste into biogas and organic manure. Department of Atomic Energy is interacting with the
Municipalities/State Governments, Ministry of Urban Development, Ministry of Non-conventional
Energy Sources and various other end-users in the public and private sectors. About 50
entrepreneurs have bought the technology document.
It is expected that units of 1,2, 5 and 10 ton per day capacities would be ideal for rural
areas and urban local bodies in the country. Thirty such NISARGRUNA plants are already operating
in various States and many more are in the process of being installed.
The Technology Transfer and Coordination Division of BARC is strongly promoting these
two technologies in rural as well as urban areas as applicable. For this purpose continuous
interactions are on with municipal bodies, industries, private entrepreneurs, local self Government
departments of State Governments, and NGOs active in rural areas. This activity is a part of
specially conceptualized initiatives such as AKRUTI (Advance Knowledge and Rural Technology
Implementation), KRUTIK (Knowledge and Rural Technology Implementation Kendra) and FORCE
(Farmers Organization for Rural Creative Entrepreneurship). Radiation Technology Development
Section and Nuclear Agriculture and Biotechnology Division of BARC shall be providing the
scientific and technological inputs for this propagation of these technologies.
Comments
The Committee commends the efforts of the Department in developing technologies
for societal benefit besides its main activities in the field of atomic energy research and hopes
that such urban waste disposal technologies would be popularized throughout the country.
Recommendation (Para 13.4)
The Committee is of the view that the need for exploring and extracting uranium from
reserves available in the country assumes utmost importance in the context of attaining greater self-
reliance for the country’s nuclear programme. The Committee, therefore, recommends that priority
be given towards this.

10
Action Taken by the Government
During the Tenth plan period, Atomic Minerals Directorate for Exploration and Research
(AMD) had implemented seven plan projects with the approved Tenth plan outlay of Rs.107.00 crore.
The project “Augmentation of Uranium Resources” has successfully been implemented and
2433 tonnes (te) of additional uranium resources in Wahkyn (1681 te) and Lostoin (752 te),
Meghalaya was established. Heliborne Frequency Domain surveys were carried out over parts of
Gwalior basin, Madhya Pradesh and North Delhi Fold belt, Rajasthan and Haryana. Many potential
areas were identified in parts of Bhima, Gwalior, Vindhyan, Chhattisgarh and other Proterozoic and
Phanerrozoic basins of India for further investigations. The procurement of the heliborne Time
Domain Electromagnetic (TDEM) Geophysical survey system and exploratory mining at Gogi,
Karnataka are in progress. Technology Demonstration Pilot Plant (TDPP) has been commissioned
at Uranium Corporation of India Limited, Jaduguda and flow sheet for processing of Tummallapalle
ore using industrial oxygen as an oxidant has been developed under the project “Technology
Demonstration and Infrastructure Development”.
The projects (i) Evaluation and Augmentation of Rare Metal and Rare Earth and Beach Sand
Heavy Mineral Resources with the identification of many potential rare metal bearing pegmatities
and recovery of 19.185 te of columbite-tantalite concentrate and establishment of India’s biggest
beach sand heavy mineral deposit containing 120 million te of heavy mineral resources out of
which 60 million te is that of ilmenite at Brahmagiri, Puri district, Orissa. The envisaged target of
another project “Contract drilling for Uranium Exploration” has also been successfully achieved
with the establishment of 13,811 te of additional uranium resources at Rohil, Rajasthan: 2953 te;
Gogi, Karnataka: 3818 te; Koppunuru: 1240 te and Chitrial, Andhra Pradesh: 5800 te against the
target of 10,000 te. A total of 68,241 m of drilling was completed against a target of 1,36,000 m.
The target of contract drilling could not be achieved due to socio-economic/naxalite problem in
Andhra Pradesh, poor infrastructure facilities and logistics problem in Meghalaya and technical
problem (borehole deviation and drift) in Rajasthan. The project is being continued in Eleventh plan
to achieve the physical targets.
The Eleventh Plan programme of AMD envisages several projects aiming to identify 75,000
tonnes of uranium resources. During Eleventh plan, AMD would be implementing 18 plan projects
with the Eleventh plan outlay of Rs. 549.19 Crore. The main emphasis is being given to extensive
survey and exploration for locating high grade large tonnage unconformity related, hematite breccia
complex, quartz pebble conglomerate (QPC), sandstone and calcrete types of uranium deposits.
High tech technique like heliborne Time Domain Electromagnetic (TDEM) survey is being adopted,
for locating deep seated concealed unconformity related deposits in the Proterozoic Basins of India.
This technique is useful in locating deep seated electromagnetic conductor which is suitable
location for high grade large tonnage unconformity related uranium deposits as in Canada and
Australia and many Proterozoic Basins in India have similar geological setup.
The detailed project proposals have since been formulated accordingly and targets for
various activities have been set up, which are about 4 to 5 times higher as compared to Tenth Plan
programme. In order to achieve the desired objectives, thrust areas like Proterozoic Basins are
selected to identify concealed large tonnage; high grade unconformity related uranium deposits apart
from other areas like Mahadek Basin for sandstone type, North Delhi Fold Belt for vein/albitite type.
The R&D sector projects includes a comprehensive set of uranium exploration activities
including airborne geophysical survey (4.0 lakh line km), ground geological and radiometric (30,000
sq. km), geochemical (8,000 sq. km) and geophysical surveys (as per requirement) and
departmental reconnoitory and stratigraphic drilling (3.0 lakh m) with the expected outcomes of
discoveries of promising uranium occurrences and evaluation and prioritization of potential target

11
areas for detailed subsurface exploration. The I&M Sector project includes detailed subsurface
exploration through contracts for evaluation drilling of 4.3 lakh m which is expected to have a
outcome of augmenting the uranium resources of the country by 75,000 tonnes.
All the activities proposed, especially with regard to uranium exploration are interdependent
and synergistically welded together so as to realize the overall Eleventh plan objectives of AMD,
the most important of which is identification of 75,000 tonnes of uranium deposits.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and hopes that sustained efforts would be made
towards exploration/mining of uranium deposits within the country, to reduce dependence on
external sources.
Recommendation (Para 14.3)
The Committee is of the opinion that awareness regarding health hazards should be created
in the affected population before the mining activity starts and therefore recommends that mass
awareness campaigns should be conducted at regular intervals for the population residing near the
mining area. The issue of displacement of the local population and sufficient compensation for the
displaced, should also be dealt with sympathetically to avoid public discontentment at a later stage.
Action Taken by the Government
An intensive Public Awareness Programme is already being carried out by the Department
of Atomic Energy (through its Public Awareness Division) in collaboration with Uranium
Corporation of India Limited and Atomic Minerals Directorate for Exploration and Research in the
areas where uranium mining is proposed. These activities are being given further impetus. Specially
in Meghalaya, a mass contact programme in Khasi language is being launched which will consist
of distribution of pamphlets, providing scientific information through games made available on CDs,
seminars in Khasi language, quiz, essay and elocution competitions. Since last more than one year,
a primary Health Centre is being run by the Uranium Corporation of India Limited at Wahkaji in
the West Khasi Hills where we propose to set up uranium mine and processing plant. An integrated
rural development programme for the six villages in the immediate neighbourhood of Jaduguda,
Jharkhand is being carried out by Uranium Corporation of India Limited and the Department. The
Department ensures that the recommendations of the Committee is implemented in letter and spirit.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and reiterates that a greater sensitivity towards the
issue of displacement of local population due to mining activities be adopted by the
Department.
Recommendation (Para 15.6)
The Committee is of the opinion that Nuclear Energy is a very clean source of energy
devoid of any environmental pollution that the production of Thermal or Hydel energy causes.
Therefore, conscious efforts should be made to produce the maximum amount of energy from
Nuclear sources.
Action Taken by the Government
Nuclear Power Corporation of India Limited (NPCIL) is involved in the first stage

12
programme of setting up a total Pressurised Heavy Water Reactors (PHWR) capacity of 10,000
MWe. Nuclear Power Corporation of India Limited has been making all efforts towards this end
and has achieved several milestones in this endeavor. At present, a PHWR capacity of 3800 MWe
is in operation and 660 MWe under construction. The operation of nuclear power plants at high
capacity factors of about 90% and construction of nuclear power projects in about five years have
been achieved. The operational and safety performance of NPCIL’s plants have been excellent.
Nuclear Power Corporation of India Limited’s current plans include setting up of eight
indigenous PHWRs of 700 MWe each. The design of indigenous 700 MWe PHWRs has been
completed. Pre-project activities for four of the reactors, KAPP 3&4 and RAPP 7&8 are nearing
competion and the projects are poised for launch. Commencement of work on these projects is
linked to establishment of fuel linkages.
The second stage of Indian nuclear power programme consists of Fast Breeder Reactors
(FBRs). FBR programme can sustain a generation capacity of about 42231 GWe – year and expected
to provide energy security to our country in the long run. Bhartiya Nabhikiya Vidhyut Nigam Limited
is constructing 500 MWe Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor (PFBR) at Kalpakkam. PFBR is the
forerunner of the second stage of India’s nuclear power programme and represents the
commencement of the commercial phase of the second stage. By constructing and operating the 500
MWe PFBR, India will be demonstrating techno-commercial viability of the second stage nuclear
power programme. It is planned to construct four more 500 MWe FBRs by year 2020. Indira Gandhi
Centre for Atomic Research will also initiate R&D design activities for 1000 MWe FBRs.
Comments
The Committee is of the opinion that the department should be able to achieve the
targets/schedules set, as regards the nuclear power projects and maximize nuclear power
generation in the near future.
Recommendation (Para 16.3)
The Committee is of the opinion that to gain self-sufficiency in the country’s requirement
of nuclear fuel, the Department has to make concerted efforts towards development of technology
which uses Thorium as Nuclear fuel instead of Uranium, keeping in view the vast reserves of
Thorium. The use of Uranium makes the country dependent on other countries and also results in
outgo of foreign exchange.
Action Taken by the Government
The three stages of the Indian Nuclear Power Programme are to be taken up sequentially.
The first stage is based on uranium and is already in commercial domain. The spent fuel from the
first stage reactors is reprocessed to recover plutonium and depleted uranium. The recovered
plutonium – depleted uranium is the fuel for the Fast Breeder Reactors for the second stage. Fast
Breeder Reactors produce more fissile material than they consume and thereby enable growth in
nuclear reactor installed capacity based on fast reactors. Physics characteristics of thorium can
enable sustaining a given installed capacity, but not its growth. Early deployment of thorium would
slow down growth of installed nuclear capacity based on fast reactors and is not desirable. While
it is proposed to set up an Advanced Heavy Water Reactor (AHWR) which would get 2/3rd of its
power from thorium, to acquire industrial scale experience in thorium, large scale introduction of
thorium has to wait till a large enough fast reactor installed capacity has been set up.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply of the Department.

13
Recommendation (Para 17.2)
The Committee expresses its serious concern at the fact that the present remuneration being
paid to the scientists is not attractive enough to attract the best of scientific talent available in the
country. Further, to make matters worse, there is a high level of attrition of scientists from the
department, who move towards the private sector for better salaries and promotion prospects. The
Committee recommends that the case for grant of special allowance over and above the normal
salaries may be taken up emphatically with the Government, keeping in view the special
requirements of the department, and the scientific community at large, specially in view of the
tremendous contributions of the scientists in the field of Atomic Energy.
Action taken by the Government
The concerns expressed by the Committee have already been taken up at appropriate levels
in the Government.
Comments
The Committee strongly reiterates its recommendation and urges that the issue of
proper remuneration for the scientist be given top priority and taken up forcefully with the
Government.
Recommendation (Para 18.5)
The Committee is of the opinion that the agreement with the United States of America has
to be looked at from the larger perspective of national security as well as national interest. While
acknowledging the increasing energy requirements of the country, the thrust must be on the
indigenous ‘Three-stage Programme’ on which our scientists are working with great confidence
and optimism. The Indo-United States Nuclear Agreement has caused serious concerns with regard
to our foreign policy and security related issues on which our Parliament had to debate several
times. The sense of the Parliament needs to be taken into consideration.
Action Taken By The Government
Indigenous three stage programme is being pursued on priority. Autonomous pursuit of our
domestic nuclear programme as well as our foreign policy would remain independent of any
international civil nuclear cooperation which would be an additionality to strengthen our energy
security.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and hopes that the domestic nuclear programme will
not be compromised in pursuit of international civil nuclear co-operation.
