1
REPORT
The Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Department of Science
and Technology on the recommendations contained in the Two Hundred Twenty-third Report of the
Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Science and Technology, Environment and
Forests on the Demands for Grants (2012-2013) of the Department of Science and Technology,
which was presented to both the Houses of Parliament on 18 th May. 2012. There were twenty-one
recommendations in the Report of the Committee. Action Taken notes on the recommendations of
the Committee were received from the Department on 21 st August, 2012.
The Committee’s recommendations, action taken thereon and comments of the Committee
on the action taken by the Department of Science and Technology are set out in the succeeding
paragraphs:–
Recommendation (Para 7.2)
The Committee is of the opinion that a robust monitoring mechanism is essential for
ensuring timely completion of the various projects to avoid time and cost overrun and to ensure
full utilization of allocated funds. The Committee appreciates that the Department has adopted the
Results Framework Document (RFD), with the objective of effective review of both the physical
and financial progress/achievements in implementation of policies, programmes projects of major
activities vis-à-vis  agreed targets fixed for each programme. The Committee hopes effective
monitoring of projects would lead to timely completion of projects and optimum utilization of funds
in the year 2012-13.
Action Taken by Government
The Department agrees with the Committee’s opinion to have a robust mechanism for
ensuring timely completion of various projects to avoid time and cost overrun and to ensure full
utilization of allocated funds. The Department under the Chairmanship of Secretary. DST reviews
and monitors all the plan schemes regularly on a monthly basis. Corrective actions, if any, are
taken during such meetings.
Besides regular monthly, quarterly and half yearly review of progress of implementation of
Schemes/programmes, all major activities of the Department are reflected in the Results Framework
Document and are monitored half yearly and annually. At the end of the financial year, a statement
of achievements by the Department is sent to Performance Management Division of the Cabinet
Secretariat. High Power Committee of the Cabinet Secretariat also examines the achievements of
the Department.
The Department will continue to use the monitoring and evaluation mechanism for all the
plan schemes in the year 2012-13 as well.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and hopes that the Department would effectively use
its monitoring mechanism to ensure timely completion of projects and fully utilize the funds
allocated to the Department in the Budget.
Recommendation (Para 8.2)
The Committee commends the fact that in all five years of Eleventh Plan the Department

2
has consistently given good performance of fund utilization and hopes the Department would give
even better performance of fund utilization in the Twelfth Five Year Plan.
Action Taken by Government
The Department is determined to maintain the record of full utilization of funds allocated
to it during the Twelfth Five Year Plan as well.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and hopes that the Department would also make all
out efforts to achieve the physical targets set for the Twelfth Plan Period.
Recommendation (Para 8.6)
The Committee takes note of the ongoing programmes of the Eleventh Plan period that are
proposed to be strengthened during the Twelfth Plan period and the new initiatives that are
proposed to be undertaken by die Department during the Twelfth Plan period. The Committee
appreciates the fact that though the major thrust areas of the Department continue to be
strengthening basic research and expanding Research and Development both in terms of Human as
well as Institutional capacities it has also been increasingly involving itself in diverse programmes
aimed at providing benefits of applications of Science and Technology, to the common masses. The
Committee is of the opinion that societal interventions of Science and Technology are needed to
improve the quality of life of our people and therefore such programme should be encouraged. The
Committee also approves of the special attention that has been given to nurture and bring women
scientists to the fore and hopes that the new programme named DISHA will help bring gender
parity in the field of Science and Technology and increase the contribution of women scientists to
science, technology and development.
Action Taken by Government
During its Twelfth Plan preparation the Department has proposed to strengthen the Eleventh
Plan initiatives as well as launch several new programmes. The Department agrees with the
Committee’s observations that major thrust area remains to be strengthening of basic research and
expanding R&D base both in terms of human as well as institutional capacities. Steps are being
taken to increase societal intervention of S&T to improve the quality of life of our people. Both
discovery as well as solution science are being given impetus during the Twelfth Plan period.
Special attention will be given to our women scientists under our new programme called ‘DlSHA’
to bring gender parity in S&T research and development. Attention is also being paid to support
those women scientists who have to shift to other locations in the country due to family reasons.
Comments
The Committee notes with satisfaction the initiatives of the Department in
increasing societal intervention of Science and Technology to improve the quality of life of
the common masses. The Committee hopes that ‘DISHA’ would help bring gender parity in
S&T research and development.
Recommendation (Para 9.4)
The Committee agrees with the justification given by the Department. The Committee is of
the view that increased investment in R&D including the strengthening of human and institutional

3
capacities in Science and Technology are necessary for realizing the vision of India emerging as
one of the top five knowledge powers in the World by 2030.
Action Taken by Government
The Department agrees with the observation of the Committee and will continue to work
towards increasing investments in R&D in the S&T sector which is necessary to make the country
emerge as one of the top five knowledge powers in the world by 2030.
Comments
The Committtee notes the reply.
Recommendation (Para 9.7, 9.8 and 9.9)
The Committee notes with concern that against a projected demand of Rs.3905.00 crores
in 2012-13 (Plan) for B.E. 2012-13, a meager amount of Rs.2477.00 crores (Plan) was actually
received by the Department, signaling a fall of Rs.1428.00 crores than the projected demand
resulting in non-institution of some the important proposed programmes.
The Committee observes that this is a very serious issue as some of the proposed important
projects will either be not taken up or would be delayed which will not be in national interest. The
Committee, therefore, recommends that the Department should pursue the case of higher
allocations with the Ministry of Finance and the Planning Commission so that the pending amount
of Rs. 1428.00 crores would be allocated to it during the R.E stage of 2012-13.
The Committee is further of the opinion that at least the Scientific Departments should be
spared from the routine cuts both at B.E and R.E stages. The Committee feels that the budgetary
cuts not only hamper the smooth progress of the projects/ Programmes, but also demoralize the
dedicated scientists who are involved in such projects.
Action Taken by Government
The Department will have to reconsider its priorities in implementing the existing projects
or initiating new projects in view of the scarcity of resources.
The Department is equally concerned with the reduction of allocation of funds proposed for
several programmes/schemes and will pursue the case for higher allocation with the Ministry of
Finance and the Planning Commission during R.E. stage of 2012-13.
The Department agrees with opinion of the committee that the Scientific Departments
should be spared from the routine cuts both at B.E. and R.E. stages. It definitely affects the
smooth progress of the projects/programmes and moral of dedicated scientists.
Comments
The Committee reiterates its concern that the Ministry of Finance has reduced the
allocation of the Department despite the fact that the Department has consistently given
good performance of fund utilization in all the five years of Eleventh Plan. It feels that the
initiatives of the Department should be encouraged, if the country has to emerge as one
of the top five knowledge powers in the world by 2030. The Committee hopes that the
Ministry of Finance/Planning Commission will favourably consider the case of higher
allocation at R.E. level so that the Department could carry out its proposed programmes/
projects smoothly.

4
Recommendation (Para 10.5)
The Committee is of the opinion that formation of a body, such as the Science and
Engineering Research Board (SERB), to coordinate and to give a renewed boost to the declining
State of  research in the basic science, was long overdue. A need for de-bureaucratization of the
Scientific departments and providing functional autonomy to the bodies engaged in  research has
long been felt by the Committee. In this direction the Committee welcomes the efforts of the
Department in the formation of the SERB, with administrative and financial autonomy of the Board
in implementing the basic research programmes efficiently and on a real time scale. The Committee
hopes that the SERB will enhance S&T capabilities of the country and lead to increased visibility
of the Indian scientists and Indian research establishments globally.
Action Taken by Government
The Science and Engineering Research Board (SERB), a Statutory body under the Department
of Science and Technology has started implementing R&D programmes with vigour. Close to Rs. 172
crores had been spent in the later half of 2011-12 by the Board and several high value nationally
important R&D projects have been implemented in a short span of its existence. A broad based
planning within the available resources has been made to implement the basic research programmes
efficiently on a real time scale. A large number of R&D projects including those of young scientists
have been sanctioned in 2012-13 wherein the allocation of the Board stands at Rs. 400.0 crore.
Directional changes like rationalization of budget heads, constitution of Peer Review Mechanisms etc.
have already been brought out in the Board. An extensive planning has been made for the Twelfth
Plan period which includes introduction of new schemes namely, Overseas Doctoral Fellowship,
Overseas Postdoctoral Fellowship, Start-Up Research Grant for Indian Diaspora, Establishment of
Joint (virtual) Centres and Challenge Award for Global Positioning. These coordinated activities of the
Board would enhance S&T capabilities of the country and lead to increased visibility of the Indian
scientists and Indian research establishments globally.
Comments
The Committee notes that the SERB has taken for implementation several high
value nationally important R&D projects and has extensive plans for the Twelfth Plan period
to project the visibility of Indian scientists and research establishments on the global
platform. The Committee hopes that the concerted efforts of the SERB would result in
giving the much desired boost to research in basic sciences in India.
Recommendation (Para 10.7)
The Committee expresses serious concern at the low level of investment in the R&D Sector
by the private sector which at present stands at only 0.25% compared to levels of 1.2 – 2.0% of
GDP in many developed and emerging economies. The Committee feels that if India has to emerge
as a scientifically developed nation that private sector investment in R&D has to increase
substantially from the present levels. This calls for greater partnership between the industries and
academia, particularly research institutions and universities. The Committee feels that the
Department should formulate such policies and programmes which would encourage the private
sector to invest substantially in the R&D sector. The private sector should be enlightened about the
advantages that would accrue to them in long term, besides financial benefits, to encourage their
participation in the country’s progress in the scientific field.
Action Taken by Government
The Department agrees with the concern expressed by the Committee to enhance the level

5
of investment in R&D by the private sector. The new Science, Technology and Innovation Policy
being formulated by the Department lays special emphasis on greater partnership among the various
sectors, such as industries, academia, research institutions and the Government to create a viable
innovation ecosystem in the country. Several programmes are being envisaged during the Twelfth
plan period for increased engagement of private sector in R&D through PPP mode in areas such
as water, climate change, energy, affordable health care, etc. Further studies are being initiated to
enhance insights for improving R&D infrastructure in industries as well as research institutions and
to evolve new PPP models for catalysing R&D for the scientific advancement in the country.
Comments
The Committee hopes that the new Science, Technology and Innovation policy would
result h1 increased engagement of private sector and enhance the level of investment by
the private sector in R&D.
Recommendation (Para 11.5)
The Committee appreciates the Department for initiating the Technology Development
Programme which aims at developing the need based indigenous technologies through joint
participation with the industry on one hand and the socio-economic Ministries on the other. The
Committee feels that the programme will help in enhancing the technological prowess of the
country. It also notes that the thrust areas of the programme which inter-alia include technology
needs for North-Eastern States, technology convergence for the production of Sulfate of Potash
are of immense importance. The Committee hopes that the Department will strive hard to make the
programme achieve its objectives. The Committee further recommends that the Department should
initiate more such programmes for the socio-economic development of the common man.
Action Taken by Government
The observation of the Committee has been noted for compliance.
Comments
The Committee hopes that the Technology Development Programme would be given
sufficient thrust, specially for the development of need based indigenous technologies for
the remote areas of the country like the North-East.
Recommendation (Para 12.5)
The Committee notes that there has been an increase of Rs.16.80 crores in B.E. 2012-13
as compared to R.E. 2011-12 under the head of International Cooperation. The Committee is of the
opinion that the need of the hour is to forge new international Science and Technology initiatives/
agreements to help bridge the Science and Technology gaps in the frontier areas of Science and
Technology, besides ensuring sharing of expertise, cost and optimal utilization of resources. The
Committee therefore, supports the programmes and hopes Department would work towards
realization of the objectives of the programme in right earnest.
Action Taken by Government
The following International S&T Cooperation activities have been already been initiated and
launched by the Department with the partner countries:
• Indo-US Endowment Fund for Innovation

6
• Outgoing Fellowship with Australia and South Korea
• Establishment of Indo-Russian Scientific and Technology Centre
• Innovation led R&D Programme with Germany. Canada and Israel
• Significant joint projects in Grand Challenge areas with UK, Australia and Spain.
• Incoming Fellowship from Myanmar
Other activities are being finalized with respective partner countries.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and hopes that more such new initiatives/agreements
would he forged with the nations having advanced Science and T echnology programmes.
Recommendation (Paras 13.4, 13.5, 13.6 and 13.7)
The Committee notes with serious concern, the lackadaisical approach adopted by the
Department towards a crucial programme such as the ‘Drugs and Pharmaceuticals Research
Programme. It notes that there are overlapping grant of loans and schemes being implemented by
Departments of Biotechnology and Scientific and Industrial Research, providing grants/soft loans on
more attractive terms to pharma industry, which has resulted in a decline in demand for the ‘Drugs
and Pharmaceutical Research’ scheme run by the Department of Science and Technology and
consequent decrease of funds’ allocated under the programme. The Committee feels that this is a
serious case of lack of coordination between the three departments viz; DST, DBT and DSIR.
which incidentally function under the same Ministry.
In this connection, Committee would a1so like to point out that in its 162
nd report on
‘Drugs and Pharmaceutical Research Programme including Herbal Medicines (Para 2.5.5. page 3),
it has been that  wide fluctuations were noticed in allocation made by the Department for ‘Drugs
and Pharmaceutical Research’. While the allocation stood at Rs.150.00 crores in RE. 2005-06. this
was reduced to Rs. 105.50 crores in R.E. 2005-06 and again increased to Rs.130.00 crores in B.E.
2006-07. It is very surprising to the Committee that a programme of the nature of ‘Drugs and
Pharmaceuticals Research’, which assumes paramount importance as it phenomenally contributes to
strategic innovations in medical sector, has been given a allocation of only Rs.60.00 crores in RE.
2011-12, which was drastically reduced to Rs.40.00 crores in B.E. 2012-13. The extent of drastic
decrease in fund allocation under this programme would be evident when present allocation are
compared to allocation six or seven years back which were of the tune of Rs.130 crores to Rs.150
crores. This is despite the prevailing general inflation over the years.
The Committee finds that the logic of the Department is strange, that their programme is
losing its importance as programmes developed by other Departments are more attractive. In the
first place, a coordinated approach ought to have been adopted by all the Departments of the
Government so as to ensure that there is no overlapping between the programmes offered by the
different departments. Secondly, the Department ought to have made its continuing programme as
attractive, if not more attractive than the similar programmes devised by the other Departments.
The Department, it seems, is simply allowing an important programme to slip out of its hands.
The Committee is of the considered view that in a country where poverty is rampant and
sizeable part of population suffers from critical diseases, continued support to drug research
programmes is the social responsibility of the Government for providing affordable drugs/
medicines to the poor masses and this responsibility cannot be diluted or absolved at any stage
through reduced allocations. The Committee feels that for a focused approach the ‘Drugs and

7
Pharmaceutical Research Programme’ should preferably be, promoted by a single Department and
the programme should be regulated in such a manner that there is no overlapping of schemes/loan
grants of the various departments. The Committee further recommends that the various
Departments may however pool their scientific expertise to achieve success of the ‘Drugs and
Pharmaceutical Research Programme’.
Action Taken by Government
The observations of the Committee have been noted for compliance. Inter-departmental
consultations among the DST, DBT & DSIR of the Ministry of Science and Technology will be
organized to bring more coordination and focused approach in Drugs and Pharmaceuticals Research
oriented Programmes implemented by these Departments, so that every Department’s programme
caters to the different needs of the end users (institutes/academia/industry) or regulated in such a
manner that there is no overlapping schemes/loan/grants of the various departments. Depending on
the outcome of these consultations, the Drugs & Pharmaceuticals Research Programme of
Department of Science and Technology will be strengthened further to meet the larger interest of
the country.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply of the Ministry and hopes that the consultation would
be completed at the earliest and concrete steps would be taken to strengthen the
programme before the end of this financial year.
Recommendation (Para 14.4)
The Committee expresses its serious concern at the waning of interest among the new
generations towards a career in science, which has led to the shortage of quality scientific and
technical manpower for the country’s scientific and research programmes. The Committee
appreciates the fact that a significant amount of Rs. 400.00 crores has been allocated for the
Alliance and R&D Mission which inter-alia aims towards attracting and encouraging the new
generation towards a research career in science. The Committee feels that the long term
requirement of generation of quality manpower needs to be addressed at different levels by
aggressively upgrading the infrastructure in universities in the field of science and promoting quality
research in them. In this direction the INSPIRE and SHE schemes, which on one hand, aim
towards inculcating an interest towards science amongst the young generation and the BEST
scheme which aims at elevating the professional and teaching skills of the teachers, by providing
them an opportunity for gaining global experience of superior methods of mentoring and teaching,
are highly commendable. The Committee feels that through such schemes the brightest students of
the country can be nurtured and retained for research in science streams and would eventually
enable India to embark on ambitious course of scientific wealth creation.
Action Taken by Government
Building of Educators for Science Teaching (BEST) scheme, aimed at elevating the
professional and teaching skills of the teachers, is being worked out. A concept note has been
preferred. The scheme is to be operated jointly by Ministry of Human Resource Development
(MHRD) and Ministry of Science and Technology (MOST). Creation of new human capacity for
pedagogy-innovation, opportunities for professional updating and exposure to superior methods of
teaching/learning from global best practices and exchange of visits to some leading centres of
science teaching are being envisaged. The sizing and scoping of the scheme would be aimed at
100% coverage of all primary, middle and secondary schools as well as colleges. The benefits of

8
the scheme proposes to reach at least 25% of all potential education targets within Twelfth Plan
period. At least 0.5 million teachers would be targeted in first phase. Active engagement of
scientific community for content and connectivity to international learning centres would be called
for. The main feature of the scheme is contemplated to spot and invest into motivated in-service
teachers already engaged in primary and secondary education and to expose them to various and
superior methods of teaching in the world without affecting their educational responsibilities.
Innovation in Science Pursuit for Inspired Research (INSPIRE), an innovative and flagship
programme designed and initiated by the Department of Science and Technology with the objective

Comments
The Committee notes with satisfaction the steps taken by the Department to build
up technical manpower to cater to growing needs of the scientific and research programmes.
In this direction, the Committee hopes that the proposed scheme of the Ministry of Science
and Technology in coordination with the Ministry of Human Resource Development, to
create new human capacities at the school level and the plans that are envisaged for the
Twelfth Plan period through various Inspire components to attract the talented youth viz.
Inspire award, Inspire Internship/Fellowship, SHE etc. would achieve the desired results.
The Committee, however, would like the Ministry to ensure that awards/fellowships are
given to only deserving and meritorious students with a view to promote building of capacity
in Science & Technology and there is no misuse of funds under the scheme.
Recommendation (Para 14.5)
The Committee also commends the initiatives of the Ministry in exploring the Public Private
Partnership (PPP) mode of funding for R&D in order to stimulate the private sector investments
into science; the PAN India S&T missions which inter-alia aims towards providing solutions of
basic problems of the common man such as food and nutrition, affordable health care and water
security and the Climate Change Programme which will focus towards the pressing issue of
Climate change. The Committee would. However, like to caution the Department to ensure the
effective implementation of these commendable programmes so that targeted benefits actually flow
from these programmes.
Action Taken by Government
To enhance the PPP mechanism under National Mission for Strategic Knowledge on Climate
Change (NMSKCC), Department of Science and Technology has organized a stakeholder meet in
collaboration with Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) and invited major industrial houses, who
have shown interest to work on key Socio-economic sectors related to climate change viz. water,
agriculture, health, environment and energy. The Meeting was organized on 12
th December, 2011
and chaired by Secretary, DST. The proposals and Climate Change initiatives from industries were
presented and discussed during the meeting. Further discussion needed to identify key players and
setting up of institutional mechanism.
Comments
The Committee hopes that further steps would be taken to identify the key players
and an institutional mechanism under the ‘National Mission for Strategic Knowledge on
Climate Change’ would be set up in a time bound manner to enhance the PPP mechanism
under NMSKCC. The Committee also hopes that the Department would explore and
encourage the PPP mode of funding for Research & Development in other areas as well.
Recommendation (Para 15.2)
The Committee commends the role of the Department in initiating the DISHA scheme,
which it feels would open up ample opportunities for women S&T professionals, whose careers
are otherwise stuck or who are forced to opt out of their careers, due to familial as well as social
obligations. The Committee feels that this scheme would provide an opportunity to women
scientists to re-enter and continue working in S&T fields of their expertise and also to continue
in the field of their choice in case they have to relocate to different places. The Committee is of
the opinion that such schemes which ensure gender parity should be supported adequately through
budgetary support.

11
Action Taken by Government
In order to take the programme of ‘DISHA’ forward, the comments of all the concerned
Ministries, Departments and Authorities have been sought. On receipt of the comments, a suitable
proposal will be placed before the Expenditure Finance Committee for its consideration and
approval. During the Eleventh Five Year Plan the budget allocated for the Women Component Plan
(DISHA Programme) was Rs.200.00 crores. The proposed budget allocation for the DISHA
Programme for the Twelfth Five Year Plan has been enhanced to 350.00 crores to intensify the
gender parity initiatives Indian science.
Comments
The Committee appreciates the increase in the proposed budgetary allocation for the
women component plan of DISHA Programme for the Twelfth Five Year Plan to Rs. 350.00
crores from Rs. 200.00 crores in the Eleventh Plan, which indicates the significance the
Government attaches to the issue of gender parity in Indian science. The Committee hopes
that all the necessary proposals to take the programme of ‘DISHA’ forward would be
finalized expeditiously.
Recommendation (Para 16.4)
The Committee is aware that Nano Technology is an upcoming field of science which holds
great potential specially in the field of designing, developing and application of carbon nano tubes
in many sectors including medicines. The Committee commends that one of the focussed areas of
research of programme, is in the field of nano-device based sensors, diagnostics kits, controlled
and targeted drug delivery systems, which would go a long way in the treatment of critical
diseases. The Committee also appreciates the fact that some of the technological achievements of
the Indian scientists have been patented and commercialized, even in technically advanced countries
like the United States, which proves the competence of the Indian scientists in the field of
nanotechnology. It also appreciates the support that the Department has provided to the scientists
and institutions working in the field of nanotechnology and hopes that in future, efforts would also
be directed towards programmes which directly affect the common man such as use of
nanotechnology for water purification, medical applications etc.
Action Taken by Government
The Department is thankful for the encouraging comments made by the Parliamentary
Standing Committee on the technological achievements made in the country in the field of Nano
Science and Technology. The Department had been funding projects in the field of water
purification, medical applications etc. using nanotechnology. The Department will continue to
promote projects/activities in focussed areas like development of nano-device based sensors,
diagnostics kits, etc. which will help in treatment of critical diseases and other applications. The
Department will also continue to promote programmes/activities which will affect the common man
(such as use of nanotechnology for water purification, medical applications etc.).
Comments
The Committee appreciates the activities and the achievements of the Department in
the field of Nanotechnology, which is an upcoming field of science and hopes that the
Department would more effectively fund programmes in the field of Healthcare, water
purification systems and other such programmes/applications that benefit the common man
so that impact of such programmes on the lives of the people becomes dearly visible in the
near future.

12
Recommendation (para 16.5)
The path-breaking contribution that nanotechnology offers to diverse areas, ranging from
industry to medicine, itself advocates for the fact that increased allocation under this head is a
compelling necessity, specially in view of the country’s excellent performance in this field, which
is apparent from the growth rate of 9.1% per year achieved by India in this field and the fact that
India has already emerged as the sixth major country in nano science output. The Committee,
however, is unhappy over the fact that in the year 2011-12, the Department failed to utilize
allocation of Rs. 105.00 crores made at B.E. stage, which resulted in reduction of allocation at R.E.
stage to Rs. 89.55 crores and provision of Rs. 85.00 crores in B.E. this year. The Committee
hopes that the Department would efficiently utilize the allocations made this year so that, if needed,
allocations could be raised at R.E. stage of 2012-13. The Committee recommends that budgetary
support for this important programme should be suitably raised at R.E. stage, so that the
programme does not suffer for want of adequate funds.
Action Taken by Government
The Department had projected a requirement of Rs.125.00 crore for 2012-13. The B.E. for
2012-13, however, is Rs.  85.00 crore. As recommended by the Parliamentary Standing Committee,
the Department will take necessary steps to launch even more ambitious projects/programmes in
high priority areas of Nano Science and Technology and seek increase in the budget at the R.E.
stage.
Comments
The Committee notes the commitment of the Department to launch more ambitious
plans in the high priority areas of Nanotechnology and hopes that the Department would
make determined efforts to secure higher allocations at RE. stage and further ensure full
and proper utilization of the allocated funds.
Recommendation (Para 17)
The Committee after examining the various aspects of the Demands for Grants (2012-13)
of the Department of Science and Technology is of the view that the Department, through its
various schemes and programmes, apart from promoting research in basic science and technology
is also taking initiative to use technology to benefit the masses. Some of the initiatives of the
Department discussed above are commendable and if properly implemented will bring immense
benefits to the targeted groups. The Department during its interaction with the Committee appeared
largely satisfied with the funds allocated for its various programmes. The Committee, while taking
note of it, is of the opinion that programmes for societal benefits and for securing bright future
for our country men should be adequately funded and hopes that in case the Department needs
more funds at R.E stage, the Planning Commission and Ministry of Finance should give due
consideration to its proposals for enhancement of funds.
Action Taken by Government
The Department respects feeling of the august Committee and will pursue the case with the
Planning Commission and Ministry of Finance for restoring proposed allocation of funds at R.E stage.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and hopes that the Department would make sincere
and determined efforts to fully achieve the targets of its various programmes.

REPORT
The Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Ministry of Environment
and Forests on the recommendations contained in the Two Hundred and Twenty Fourth Report
of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Science and Technology,
Environment and Forests on the Demands for Grants (2012-13) of the Ministry of Environment
and Forests, which was presented to both the Houses of Parliament on 18
th May, 2012. There
were thirty one recommendations in the Two Hundred and Twenty Fourth Report of the
Committee. Action Taken notes on the recommendations of the Committee were received from
the Ministry on 17
th September, 2012.
The Committee’s recommendations, action taken thereon and comments of the Committee
on the Action Taken by the Ministry of Environment and Forests are set out in the subsequent
paragraphs:–
Recommendation (Para 6.5)
The Committee, hopes that the Ministry would not only be able to get full allocation of its
approved budgetary support during the Twelfth Five Year Plan, but would also ensure full utilization
of funds allocated to it and it would not come to the Committee with the same old excuses for
not fully utilizing the allocated funds.
Action Taken by Government
The Ministry of Environment and Forests has proposed an outlay of Rs 47856 crore for
its Twelfth Five Year Plan, 2012-17. Detailed scheme/programme wise justification has been
provided to the Planning Commission on such enhanced fund requirements of the Ministry during
the Annual Plan 2012-13 discussions with the Commission. However, the Twelfth Five Year Plan
Document, and corresponding plan outlays for various Ministries, is yet to be finalized by the
Planning Commission. The recommendation of the Committee has been communicated to the
Commission for their consideration and necessary action on fund requirements/demand of the
Ministry.
Various measures have been taken by the Ministry in recent past to ensure utilization of
funds allocated to it. This, inter alia , include streamlining formulation and implementation
mechanism of schemes to enable faster disbursement of funds to the states; undertaking fresh
appraisal of the schemes to provide transparency and outcome orientation; revising guidelines
towards harmonization of cost norms in respect of various components, identification of core/
non core activities; putting in place suitable monitoring mechanisms for receipt of proposals from
and release of funds to states; and effecting other changes in the Centrally Sponsored Schemes
towards ensuring faster and transparent release/utilization of funds by the states. Release of
grants through new mechanisms has/is been developed like the mechanism of State Forest
Development Agency (SFDA) for releases under the National Afforestation Programme (NAP)
scheme. Improvements have also been effected in institutional mechanisms, like setting up of the
National Mission Clean Ganga, to expedite implementation of schemes. The Ministry also prepares
an Outcome Budget defining the outcomes, scheme-wise, in terms of measurable and monitorable
deliverables, which are regularly reviewed. Inclusion of the Ministry under in Modified Cash
Management System w.e.f. 2012-13 would also facilitate better financial planning and proper and
effective utilization of funds.

2
These measures, besides facilitating faster implementation of the schemes/sub-schemes of
the Ministry, would also ensure optimal utilization of their allocations. It is felt that the Ministry
has the necessary absorption capacity and other infrastructural and institutional mechanisms in
place to undertake implementation of its plan proposals during 2012-13 and Twelfth Five Year Plan.
Ministry will make all out efforts to utilize fully the funds allocated to it by the Planning
Commission during the Twelfth Five Year Plan.
Comments
The Committee takes note of the action taken and hopes that as a result of
measures taken, Ministry would be able to meet its various targets during 2012-13 and
would be able to fully utilize the funds allocated to the Ministry in the year 2012-13.
Recommendation (Para 6.9)
The Committee is happy to note that the Ministry has, at the instance of Planning Commission
and the Finance Ministry rationalized its schemes/programmes through merger/clubbing and has been
able to bring down the number of schemes from 22 in the Eleventh Five Year Plan to 18 in the
Twelfth Five Year Plan. The Committee is of the view that integration of programmes through
rationalization helps the Ministry to focus its attention on the programmes in an effective, efficient
and result oriented manner. But, at the same, the Committee feels that the smaller sub-schemes after
getting integrated with a major scheme or programme does not attract as much attention and hence
it’s monitoring and performance gets affected. The Committee, therefore, recommends that while
monitoring the major projects/schemes, the Ministry must ensure that performance of the smaller sub-
schemes is not lost sight of and must ensure that progress and performance of smaller schemes is
also regularly monitored, particularly, the component of wetlands, scheme of corals and mangroves
as these are different from monitoring an inland lake or river.
Action Taken by Government
As per guidelines of the Planning Commission and the Finance Ministry, the Plan schemes
of the Ministry have been further rationalized by suitable merger/clubbing of smaller schemes under
broader thematic or Umbrella schemes. Such a rationalization has resulted in reduction of Ministry’s
total thematic schemes from 22 in the Eleventh Plan to 18 in the Twelfth Plan. However, none of
the smaller schemes has been dropped, and their individual identity has been retained by designating
them as separate sub-schemes under an Umbrella scheme. Thus, the Umbrella scheme of
“Conservation of Natural Resources and Ecosystems” includes, as sub-schemes, Programmes on
Lakes, Wetlands, Mangroves and Corals to ensure progress and performance of these sub-schemes/
programmes. These specific sub-schemes will continue to address the target area or activity as
earlier with enhanced funds, streamlined implementation through updated guidelines and revision of
scheme consequent upon its evaluation/appraisal.
Performance of the schemes is reviewed by the Secretary regularly in Senior Officers
meeting of the Ministry. Review meetings are also undertaken at Minister level. Planning
Commission conducts Half Yearly review meetings with the Ministry, to monitor progress of
various schemes/projects. Further, Ministry has designated its senior officers as Nodal officers for
each state/UT, and these Nodal officers visit their designated states/UTs regularly to, inter alia ,
monitor and review progress of schemes/projects in these states/UTs. Subject Divisions in the
Ministry executing/implementing the schemes also undertake regular field visits to carry out
performance review of the schemes. Finally, Regional offices of the Ministry review/monitor and
follow up on various issues/programmes in the environment, forestry and wildlife sectors. To
review performance of smaller schemes like wetlands, mangroves, corals etc. appropriate

3
Committees have been set up at National and State levels under the sub-schemes to identify, review
and monitor the progress under these sub-schemes.
Comments
The Committee takes note of the reply and hopes that as a result of robust
monitoring/review mechanism, put in place by the Ministry it shall be able to meet its
targets and utilize fully and efficiently funds allocated to it under various schemes in the
year 2012-13.
Recommendation (Para 7.2)
The Committee is surprised to note that the Twelfth Five Year Plan for the Ministry is yet
to be finalized by the Planning Commission even when the first year of the Five Year Plan has set
in. The Committee expresses its serious concern over delay in finalization of Twelfth Five Year Plan
outlays of an important Ministry engaged in protection of environment and conservation of forests,
so vital for the healthy and comfortable living of human beings. The Committee, therefore,
recommends that henceforth Planning Commission must ensure that such sort of delay does not
recur in future and outlays are finalized well before the beginning of the Plan period. The
Committee is also of the opinion that any further laxity in early finalization of Twelfth Plan outlays
may have adverse consequences on restoration of environmental degradation and control of water,
air and noise pollution in particular and therefore it should be finalized without any further delay.
The Committee is also of the opinion that environment and forests need to be accorded due priority
in the developmental agendas of the nation in view of the lurking challenges that climate change
poses before us. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the proposed outlay of Rs. 47586.00
crore of the Ministry should be given serious consideration by the Planning Commission, so as to
ensure availability of adequate funds to the Ministry for pursuing its avowed objectives successfully.
Action Taken by Government
The Ministry of Environment and Forests has proposed an outlay of Rs 47586 crore for
its Twelfth Five Year Plan, 2012-17. Detailed scheme/programme wise justification for such
enhanced fund requirements of the Ministry have been provided to the Planning Commission during
the Annual Plan 2012-13 for discussions with the Commission. However, the Twelfth Five Year
Plan Document, and corresponding plan outlays for various Ministries, is yet to be finalized by the
Planning Commission. The concerns of the Committee have been communicated to the Commission
for their necessary action on fund requirements/demand of the Ministry.
Comments
The Committee is constrained to observe that Plan outlays for Ministry of
Environment and Forests have still not been finalized by Planning Commission despite
serious concern expressed by the Committee some six months back. The Committee takes
a very serious view on the matter and wants the Ministry to take up the matter with the
Planning Commission forcefully.
OUTLAY PROPOSED AND BUDGETARY ALLOCATION MADE FOR THE YEAR 2012-13
Recommendation (Para 8.9)
The Committee takes a very serious view on the consistent reduction in Budgetary
Allocation for such an important ministry, like, Ministry of Environment and Forests during the last
two years. The Committee also feels that if we fail to take timely action and adopt adequate

4
measures now, we will be forced to spend huge resources in not too distant future on adaptation
and mitigation measures to remedy the after-effects of climate change. The Committee notes with
concern that the share of Ministry of Environment and Forests in the Central Plan has consistently
been declining in successive Plan periods. Starting with the percentage share of 0.83% in Seventh
Plan, it came down to 0.67% in Tenth Plan and further down to 0.41% in Eleventh Plan. The share
of the Ministry in the Annual Plan 2012-13 has become a dismal 0.37%. The Committee is
constrained to observe that this is a very disturbing trend which needs to be reversed. The
Committee, therefore, recommends that Planning Commission must provide not only adequate
Budgetary Support to the Ministry of Environment and Forests at the R.E. stage of this Financial
Year, but also seriously consider substantially enhancing the percentage share of Ministry of
Environment and Forests in the Central Plan consistent with the growing importance of issues dealt
by the Ministry.
Action Taken by Government
Ministry of Environment and Forests has been consistently highlighting the lowering of its
relative priority/share in plan outlay allocations over the various Five Year Plans to the Planning
Commission despite the growing importance of environmental issues over these years. Conceding
such under provision for the Ministry/sector, Planning Commission, while reviewing the Eleventh
Five Year Plan of the Ministry, has recommended that “an allocation of at least 5% of annual, state,
and central sector outlay for the environment and forestry sectors separately needs to be ensured,
preferably by the Twelfth Plan”. [Planning Commission Mid-Term Review of Eleventh Five Year
Plan, Page 471, Para 22.97].
This concern and recommendation of the Committee has been forwarded to the Planning
Commission, which is currently in the process of finalizing the Twelfth Five Year Plan and
associated sectoral outlays.
Comments
The Committee takes note of the reply.
Recommendation (Para 8.13)
The Committee feels that the tardy trend of utilization of resources provides the Planning
Commission with an alibi to affect cut in the allocation of resources. The Committee, therefore,
recommends that the Ministry should make necessary efforts to fully utilize the allocated resources
in future, so that, Planning Commission does not take recourse to such cut measures.
Action Taken by Government
Savings in 2011-12 emerged from the late start of the Externally Aided Projects (EAP)
projects like the Coastal Zone Management Programme, National Ganga River Basin Authority
(NGRBA), Capacity Building for Industrial Pollution Management (CBIPMP), Capacity Building for
Forest Management and Training of Personnel, and the Bio-diversity Conservation and Rural
Livelihood Improvement Project, whose outlays were earmarked. Ministry’s request for re-
appropriation of these EAP savings to other non EAP projects/schemes of the Ministry with
additional demand for funds was not acceded to by the Finance Ministry. Efforts have, however,
been made in 2012-13 Plan to peg the EAP outlays on a more realistic level to ensure full utilization
of the available outlay. Ministry would further strive towards a more meticulous planning, timely
implementation and strict monitoring of the schemes/projects to ensure a more efficient utilization
of plan funds allocated to it.

5
To ensure proper and effective utilization of funds, the schemes/projects of the ministry are
being monitored regularly, both at central level as well as field level. A mechanism of Nodal
Officers has been established, under which each state/UT has been assigned a senior Officer as
its nodal officer for regular interaction with them. Major schemes of the Ministry also have an in-
built independent monitoring mechanism to ensure effective and timely utilization of funds. The
centrally sponsored schemes in the Forestry and Wildlife sector have streamlined their
implementation mechanism and release of funds to enable faster disbursement of funds to the
states. Similar changes have been effected in other Centrally Sponsored Scheme (CSS) towards
ensuring faster and transparent release/utilization of funds by the states. The Electronic Clearance
of funds for various schemes/projects is also an important improvement for ensuring a quick and
faster disbursement of funds. Further, inclusion of the Ministry in Modified Cash Management
System w.e.f. 2012-13 would also facilitate better financial planning and proper and effective
utilization of funds.
Comments
The Committee takes note of the Action Taken and hopes that the Ministry would
be able to fully utilize the allocated resources in the year 2012-13.
Recommendation (Para 8.16)
A glance at the above statement indicates that plan outlay for National Coastal Management
Programme, National River Conservation Plan, Capacity Building for Forest Management and
Training of Personnel has come down due to rationalization of Budgetary support for Externally
Aided Projects. However, lower allocation for these schemes is due to lower availability of overall
plan funds. The Committee feels that reduction in Budgetary Allocations is hardly justified, as it will
adversely affect environment and forestry activities. The Committee, therefore, recommends that
adequate budgetary support should be provided to the Ministry at the R.E level.
Action Taken by Government
Allocation of funds to various schemes of the Ministry has been dictated by the low overall
enhancement of outlay provided to the Ministry in 2012-13, which is only 5.6% over the preceding
year. Rationalization of outlays for EAP in 2012-13 has been prompted by need to avoid a recurrence
of savings under these schemes as in 2011-12. Also, given the low increase in ministry’s overall
outlay, such adjustment in EAP outlays was necessary to provide for funding of important non-EAP
schemes like the Green India Mission, Climate change and Biodiversity conservation.
The Ministry would strive towards an efficient utilization of plan funds allocated to it
towards ensuring adequate availability of funds for its various schemes/programmes. Depending
upon their actual performance in the first half of the year, and revised fund requirements of these
schemes/programmes, the issue of more funds allocation at RE stage will be taken up with the
Planning Commission/Finance Ministry, if necessary.
Comments
The Committee takes note of the reply.
CENTRAL POLLUTION CONTROL BOARD (CPCB)
Recommendation (Para 10.4)
The Committee further feels that the major constraint in effective functioning of CPCB is

6
the shortage of technical staff, scientists and lack of quality laboratory facilities. The Committee,
therefore, recommends that the Ministry should focus its attention in addressing these constraints,
so that CPCB is able to effectively discharge its duties and functions. The Committee also feels
that there is a need to improve internal working of the CPCB and its coordination with SPCBs,
etc. The Committee is of the view that CPCB should hold meetings more frequently and its
Members should regularly visit various places and hold discussion with concerned SPCBs, etc. so
as to have a firsthand experience of ground realities prevailing in the country and to sensitize the
ground functionaries to effectively discharge their duties.
Action Taken by Government
Efforts are being made to fill-up the existing technical and scientific vacancies in CPCB.
A proposal to create 102 new posts in CPCB was taken up with the Department of Expenditure
who opined that CPCB may fill-up the existing vacant posts and get revive the abolished posts
having functional requirement in the first instance and then initiate the process of creation of new
posts. As such the proposal to revive 38 deemed abolished posts in CPCB is under examination
in MoEF. After an appropriate view is taken on this issue, further action would be taken
accordingly to strengthen the manpower in CPCB. The suggestions regarding holding of Board
meetings wore frequently, field units and discussions with SPCBs have been noted for
compliance.
Comments
The Committee takes note of the reply and desires that besides manpower, technical
facilities like lab, etc. too need to be simultaneously augmented/strengthened.
Recommendation (Para 10.5)
The Committee finds that although pollution in some form or the other has spread its
wings throughout the length and breadth of the country, CPCB, in terms of its infrastructure,
manpower, etc. has not been able to keep pace with the phenomenal growth of the pollution –
industrial, vehicular, sewage and solid waste, etc. It has six zonal offices with each zonal office
covering 3 to 8 States while the number of industries, vehicular load, sewage and solid waste,
etc. has multiplied manifold in the course of time. The Committee feels that the number of zonal
offices of CPCB needs to be increased so that it is able to keep a closer watch on air, water
and noise pollution in the country. The Committee, therefore, recommends the Ministry of
Environment and Forests should consider enhancing the number of zonal offices in a phased but
time-bound manner.
Action Taken by Government
At present, Zonal Offices of CPCB are functioning at Bangalore, Bhopal, Kolkata, Shillong,
Lucknow and Vadodara, and a Project Office is functioning at Agra. The Zonal Offices are
entrusted with the responsibility to undertake environment surveillance in their areas and particularly
to verify compliance by the industries based on surprised checks. Besides, Zonal Offices play a
key role in undertaking performance studies of various common waste management facilities and
interact with SPCBs/PCCs on state-specific issues. The suggestion of the committee for enhancing
the number of Zonal Offices in the country is under examination.
Comments
The Committee takes note of the reply.

7
Recommendation  (Para 10.7)
While informing that there has been an increase in outlay over the years, the Ministry
agreed that increase in allocation of funds has not been substantial and commensurate with the need
of quantum of funds required for improving the challenges of pollution control. It further informed
that the Ministry has been emphasizing upon the Planning Commission for enhanced allocation, but
the Ministry has not been able to get the required allocation despite justification and persuasion. The
Committee takes a very serious view that despite justification and persuasion, the Planning
Commission did not allocate adequate resources for prevention and control of pollution. The
Committee recommends that sufficient budgetary allocation should be allocated under this Head by
the Planning Commission, so that the Ministry could take effective measures to deal with the ever
increasing problem of pollution.
Action Taken by Government
The matter is being taken up again with the Planning Commission for enhancement of
budget allocations to accommodate the activities of CPCB.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.
Recommendation (Para 10.8)
The Committee, however, finds that during the year 2011-12, CPCB had not been able to
utilize even the Plan budgetary allocation of Rs.40.00 crores and could only utilize Rs.30.00 crores
by 29
th February, 2012 which can be adjudged as a poor performance in terms of financial
progress. Poor financial progress had its impact on physical targets as well. Out of the 60 new
ambient air quality and 160 noise monitoring stations proposed to be established during the year,
43 ambient air quality monitoring stations could be established and the process of setting up of

Out of Plan allocation Rs.40 crores, CPCB spent Rs.38.8168 crores during 2011-2012. An

Comments
The Committee takes note of the reply but would like Ministry to ensure that, in
future, examination of projects, for which funds have been sought and earmarked, is not
unduly delayed to an extent that leads to non-utilisation of funds so earmarked.
Recommendation (Para 10.9)
The Committee feels that for effective monitoring of ambient air and water quality and
control of pollution, close coordination between CPCB, SPCBs and Pollution Control Committees
is essential. The growing levels of pollution throughout the country are however indicative of lack
of active coordination and cooperation between CPCB and SPCBs and also of their failure to
discharge their duties effectively and efficiently. The Committee was unhappy to know that State

8
Governments are not according due priority to environment and in majority of States, it is almost
a non-issue. The Committee, however, feels that for getting the desired support from SPBC/PCCs,
CPCB, first, needs to galvanize and activate itself so as to play a lead role in coordinating the
activities of State Pollution Control Boards, a function statutorily assigned to it. It should also
actively exercise its mandate to plan and cause to be executed a nationwide programme for the
prevention, control, or abatement of water and air pollution. In suitable cases, CPCB can also take
recourse to Section 18(1)(b) of the Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974, which
imposes a statutory duty on State Board to abide by the directions of the Central Board given to
it in writing, to garner necessary support from those State Pollution Control Boards who are not
discharging their assigned duties properly. The above provisions underscore the pivotal position
provided to the CPCB under the scheme of the Act to ensure effective control of pollution.
Action Taken by Government
CPCB is co-ordinating with SPCBs on various matters pertaining to abatement of pollution.
Some of the key on-going programmes being implemented in coordination with SPCBs are;
/head2rightWater and ambient air quality monitoring;
/head2rightDevelopment of standards and their enforcement through SPCBs/PCCs;
/head2rightEnvironmental quality assessment in 43 critically polluted industrial clusters;
/head2rightPollution control compliance in 17 categories of industries and for industries discharging
waste water into rivers and lakes.
With regard to control of pollution relating to sewage, municipal solid waste, plastic
waste, bio-medical waste, hazardous waste, etc., CPCB and SPCBs are not able to show
tangible results because of dependence on other implementing agencies such as
Municipalities, State Urban Development Departments and others departments. However,
CPCB is making concerted efforts toward abatement of pollution.
Comments
The Committee had desired that CPCB played a pivotal role in coordinating the
activities of SPCBs/PCCs and if needed, took recourse to Section 18(1)(b) of the Water
(Prevention & Control of Pollution) Act, 1974 to motivate/activate those who were not
performing. But the Ministry has surprisingly maintained silence on this particular issue.
The Committee, therefore, reiterates its recommendation.
Recommendation (10.10)
The Committee also understands that the Ministry is running a centrally sponsored scheme
called “Assistance for Abatement of Pollution” the objective of which inter-alia is to strengthen
SPCBs for enforcing statutory provisions for pollution abatement. The Committee feels that the
Ministry may also think of linking financial assistance with performance of SPCBs, thus
encouraging the non-performing Boards to be active in order to get financial assistance.
Action Taken by Government
The suggestion of the committee is under examination.
Comments
The Committee takes note of the reply but would like the Ministry to complete its
examination at the earliest.

9

It further added that more stringent standards have been notified for cement industries
which are being complied with. Apart from the above, CPCB is carrying out surprise checks of

Comments
The Committee notes the reply.
Recommendation (Para 10.13)
The Committee is happy to note that the Ministry proposes to establish a National
