B. PROGRAMMES OF CSIR
(I) National Laboratories Scheme
The Committee, in its 208
th Report, had recommended that the network of National
Laboratories should be extended to all the states of the country, with at least one laboratory in each
state so that there is equitable scientific progress in each State. The Committee had also
recommended that though the National Laboratories are doing a lot of ingenious work as regards
Research and Development in various scientific spheres but most of its achievements are not
reaching the common man. In fact, the Committee had felt that the Department of Scientific and
Industrial Research could justify an increase in the budgetary allocation only if substantial benefits
reach the common man and had accordingly recommended that the Department should focus
towards transfer of technology from the National Laboratories to the society.
The Department, however, in its Action Taken Note defended its stand by saying the CSIR
transferred its developed technologies regularly to industries through its constituent laboratories.
Some technology transfers at that time included improved process for centchroman (a non-steroidal
oral contraceptive); treatment of Bio refractory wastewater without sludge and odor emission.
While the Committee appreciates the fact that transfer of some technologies had taken place but
transfer of just few technologies is not going to make the desired impact. The CSIR, with a large
scientific manpower at its command, needs to transfer innovative technologies in a large number
so as to help common man improve his living standard. The CSIR must pay rich dividends to the
common citizen of this country by way of transfer of appropriate technologies for every rupee
invested in its schemes.
Action Taken by Government
During Twelfth Five Year Plan, the Department proposes to establish five new institutes.
CSIR and its constituent laboratories are home to cutting edge scientific capabilities, talent,
know-how and IP. To further enhance the capability and to explore newer models of bringing
processes, products and services to the markets, an independent company named ‘CSIR Tech
Private Limited (CTPL)’ has been incorporated in Pune. CTPL would work closely with CSIR labs

8
to commercialize CSIR technologies and intellectual property through creation of spin-outs and
licensing opportunities based on scientific discoveries emanating from CSIR laboratories.
Comments
The Committee notes the initiative taken by the CSIR to explore and to further
enhance its capabilities by incorporating a company named ‘CSIR Tech Private Limited
(CTPL) and hopes that this new venture would result in effective commercialisation of CSIR
technologies.
Recommendations
II. National S&T Human Resource Development
The Committee observes that allocation made under this head was Rs.307.00 crore at B.E.
stage 2011-12 which got slightly reduced to Rs.305.00 crore in B.E. 2012-13. The Committee finds
that out of the allocated amount of Rs.307.00 crore at B.E. 2011-12, the Department could utilize
only Rs.285.00 crore. This may, perhaps be one of the reasons for lesser allocation has been made
this year under this head. The Committee hopes that Department shall be able to make full and
effective use of funds allocated to it this year.
The Committee notes that the CSIR has introduced 250 CSIR hand holding scholarship for
dyslexic (Attention Deficit Disorder) students to pursue higher education in science. The Committee
feels that this is a very praiseworthy initiative that needs to be further extended and expanded. The
Committee therefore, recommends that this scheme should not cover only dyslexic students but
those suffering from other serious physical disabilities as well.
The Committee feels that institution of greater number of scholarship for higher studies in
science shall to certain extent help in arresting the recent trend of large number of bright students
not opting science subjects for higher studies in view of attractive opportunities that have emerged
in other disciplines and which in turn is leading to shortage of scientific personnel in the country.
The Committee, therefore, recommends that there is a need for further increasing the number of
scholarships as also for making scholarship more attractive. The Committee, further, recommends
that a very transparent, fair and objective criteria be devised for awarding these scholarships so
that meritorious students alone get it.
Action Taken by Government
The initial allocation during the financial year 2011-12 was Rs.307.00 crore (Rs.197.00
crore under Plan and Rs.110.00 crore under Non-Plan) for this head. The Department could have
utilized the allocation of Rs.307.00 crore fully and effectively, however, Ministry of Finance
imposed a cut of Rs.1 00.00 crore on Plan allocation and Rs.58.18 crore on Non-Plan allocation
on the department. Accordingly the Department imposed a cut of Rs.22.00 crore (Rs.7.00 crore
on Plan and Rs.15.00 crore on Non-Plan) for this activity thereby reducing total budgetary
allocation to Rs.285.00 crore which has been fully utilized during financial year 2011-12. Efforts
are being made to utilize the full grant allocated during the financial year 2012-13.
The recommendation of the Committee has been noted. The students suffering from other
serious physical disabilities will also to be covered under this scheme subject to getting requisite
budgetary allocation.
Efforts are being made continuously by the Department to attract more number of bright
students to opt science subjects for higher studies through various fellowship schemes. CSIR has

9
increased the number of Junior Research Fellowships (JRF) by two folds during the Eleventh Five
Year Plan period (2007-12) over the Tenth Five Year Plan (2002-07) through CSIR-UGC National
Eligibility Test (NET) scheme with regard to qualification and validity of CSIR JRF to widen the
scope of NET and to attract students at early stages of their career. CSIR has also increased the
number of Shyama Prasad Mukherjee Fellowships (SPMF) from the financial year 2012-13 which
is being offered to certain top ranking NET qualified candidates. Besides NET, CSIR has other
fellowship schemes such as JRF-GATE, Senior Research Fellowships, Research Associateships,
Senior Research Associateships and CSIR-Nehru Science Postdoctoral Research Fellowships for
attracting and retaining students in science.
A very transparent, fair and objective criterion is being followed to award the fellowships
through CSIR-UGC NET conducted twice a year with the objective to identify and nurture young
scientific talent to pursue Ph.D. programmes. NET qualified students are being sought by both
academic and R&D institutions across India.
Comments
The Committee is pleased to note that the Department has agreed to the proposal of the
Committee to widen the ambit of its 250 CSIR handholding scholarships to the students suffering
from other serious physical disabilities.

III. INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY AND TECHNOLOGY MANAGEMENT
The Committee is happy to know that CSIR’s rate of licensing/commercialization of
Intellectual Property at about 9% is much better as compared to the global average of 3-4% and
compliments CSIR for it. The Committee, however, feels that there is a need for wider and more
effective dissemination of products/technologies developed by CSIR and patents registered by it so
that common man could be benefited from this knowledge. The Department may consider making
details of all products/technologies developed by it available on its website and organizing seminars
and exhibitions in different parts of the Country to make people aware of them. Advertisements/
handbills and poster campaigns can also be deployed appropriately to create awareness.
Action Taken by Government
The Department appreciates the compliments of the Committee regarding higher rate of
licensing/ commercialization of its IP vis-a-vis  global average. In most of CSIR laboratories,
advertisement and awareness with regard to patent/technology/know-how is usually carried out
through the Institute websites, publications such as annual reports, newsletters, special pamphlets
and brochures. Patent/business development related awareness programmes are sometimes included
in short term courses/Entrepreneur Development Programme undertaken by the lab, both for the
entrepreneurs as well as students. Patents filed and granted are available in the Annual report of
CSIR.
Technology awareness meets are also arranged and users/interested manufacturers are
invited in these meets for interaction with inventors/business development groups. Technology/
know-how developed are also displayed on the Institute website. Advertisement and awareness are
also arranged through Seminars/conferences/workshops, events/exhibitions, internet networking.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply of the Department.

IV. NEW MILLENNIUM INDIAN TECHNOLOGY LEADERSHIP INITIATIVE (NMITLI)
The Committee finds that this programme was allocated Rs.70 crares at B.E. 2011-12 which
was reduced to Rs.50.00 crares at R.E. 2011-12 but again enhanced to Rs.60.00 crores at B.E. 2012-
13. Noting that programme is to be run on PPP model, the Committee hopes that the Department
would effectively leverage the funds allocated to obtain desired outcome under the scheme.
The Committee has been informed that the reason behind NMITLI Scheme not performing
as expected is that the country is not able to recognize and appreciate the concept of PPP for
Research & Development for R&D. In addition, there is no enabling mechanism to develop
seamless team between industry and publicly funded institutions. It has, further been informed that
the Department proposes to broaden the NMITLI scheme in the Twelfth Plan as per the Cabinet
Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA) approval.
The Committee is of the view that the Department should take necessary steps to dispel
the apprehensions about PPP mode and make sincere efforts to ensure success of this model.
Action Taken by Government
Fluctuations in NMITLI Budget over the years are due to following:
Funds under NMITLI are utilized timely and effectively. On occasions, Finance Ministry
imposes cut on Department’s budget at RE stage. This cut has to be borne by various programmes
of the Department including NMITLI. For example-Finance Ministry had imposed a cut of Rs.1 00
crore in the budget of CSIR at RE stage for the Financial Year 2010-11. Considering the same and
creating a possibility of funding some of the NMITLI projects in the beginning of the next Financial
year, a cut of Rs.25 crore was employed to NMITLI. It shifted thus taking up of some of newer
projects to Financial Year 2011-12 and utilized the funds within permissible time.
NMITLI is a robust Public Private Partnership (PPP) Scheme in the R&D domain in the
country. It has been able to network about 100 industry partners and about 300 R&D groups from
different institutions. Realizing the success of the model, other government departments are emulating
it. After NMITLI, PPP has become a buzz word in the echelon of Science & Technology. NMITLI
will take every possible step to further strengthen the scheme and ensure success of model.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and hopes that as assured, the Department would
further strengthen NMITLI Scheme.
Recommendation

VII. NA TIONAL CIVIL AIRCRAFT DEVELOPMENT PROGRAMME (NCAD)
The Committee hopes that formal Government approval for the programme would be
available soon and the programme would start in right earnest at the earliest. The Committee is also
of the view that this programme is of great national importance and sufficient funds be made
available to this programme so that our own indigenous 90 seater aircraft becomes a reality in a

Action Taken by Government
In order to identify an enabling (entity) structure for implementation of the National Civil
Aircraft Development (NCAD) programme, CSIR constituted two expert committees. The two
committees are as follows:
(i) Technical Committee to build NCAD programme: The said committee will examine the
feasibility Report and create a document for NCAD programme implementation. It will
also prepare a Cabinet note for obtaining ‘In-principle’ approval from the Government.
(ii) Joint Venture Creation Committee to interact and negotiate with the industry: This
committee will identify and discuss with industry for firming the Joint Venture with
equity participation in design and development and for setting up production facility
and marketing of 90 seater Civil Aircraft under NCAD programme.

Further, the NCAD programme will be taken up, in case desired partnerships are built and
due approvals are received.
Comments
The Committee hopes that the Department would be able to find a suitable partner
to take the National Civil Aircraft Development (NCAD) programme forward.
Recommendation
VIII. INTERACTION BETWEEN INDUSTRY AND CSIR
The Committee is happy to learn that CSIR has implemented all the recommendations of
Abid Hussain Committee. The Committee notes that share of public funding for R&D at 2-3 per
cent of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) is at par with international norms. However, the share of
private funds for R&D at only 3 per cent of GDP in our country is very low as compared to
international norms of 1.3-1.4 of GDP. In France, Industry performs over 63 per cent (of all R&D)
and funds around 54 per cent projects while this figure is 69 per cent in Japan. In India
contribution of industries is estimated at around 25 per cent of national R&D expenditure which
needs to be enhanced to at least 50 per cent in the Twelfth Plan. The Committee feels that the
Department should give more and more incentive and form more partnerships with the private
sector companies of India in order to infuse more funds in R&D sector. In this regard, the
Committee fully supports the recommendations of the Planning Commission in its ‘approach paper
on Twelfth Five Year Plan-Faster, Sustainable and more Inclusive Growth’ wherein it has suggested
on interaction of Public S&T Institutions with CSIR at large.
Action Taken by Government
The Department is trying to bring industries on board in many plan projects being proposed
to be executed during Twelfth Five Year Plan.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply of the Department and hopes that CSIR would soon
be able to work in partnership with other big industrial players in its endeavour to increase
the share of private funds for Research and Development activities.
Recommendation (Para 10.4)
Audit Objection
The Committee taking serious note of the above observations made by the CAG
recommends that these deficiencies need to be addressed by the Department in right earnest as
such cases bring bad repute to CSIR and this does not put DSIR in right stead. The Committee,
further, recommends that the Department should strengthen its monitoring mechanism so that
misuse of funds could be prevented.
Action Taken by Government
The observations of the Committee have been noted for compliance.
Comments
The Committee would like the Department to ensure such cases do not occur in
future and audit objection is duly settled to the satisfaction of the Comptroller and Auditor
General of India.

PREFACE
I, the Chairman of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Science
and Technology, Environment and Forests, having been authorised by the Committee to present the
Report on its behalf, present this Two Hundred Thirty Eighth Report on the Action Taken by the
Department of Biotechnology on the recommendations contained in Two Hundred Twenty Eighth
Report of the Committee on Demands for Grants (2012-13) of the Department of Biotechnology.
2. The Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Department of
Biotechnology on the recommendations contained in the Two Hundred Twenty Sixth Report of the
Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Science and Technology, Environment and
Forests on the Demands for Grants (2012-13) of the Department of Biotechnology which was
presented to the Rajya Sabha on 18
th May, 2012.
3. There were twenty-two recommendations contained in the Two Hundred Twenty Eighth
Report of the Committee. Action Taken Notes on the recommendations of the Committee were
received from the Ministry on 20
th September, 2012.
4. In the meeting held on 17 th December, 2012, the Committee considered the Draft Action
Taken Report and adopted the same.
DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY
NEW D ELHI; Chairman,
December 17, 2012 Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on
Science and Technology, Environment and Forests

ACRONYMS
BIRAC – Biotechnology Industry Research Accreditation Council
DBT – Department of Biotechnology
DCGI – Durg Controller General of India
ICGEB – International Centre for Genetic Engineering and Biotechnology
NIH – National Institute of Health
MVDP – Malaria V accine Development Programme
PPP – Public-Private-Partnership

1
REPORT
The Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Department of
Biotechnology on the recommendations contained in the Two Hundred and Twenty Eighth Report
of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Science and Technology,
Environment and Forests on the Demands for Grants (2012-13) of the Department of
Biotechnology, which was presented to both the Houses of Parliament on 18
th May, 2012. There
were twenty one recommendations in the Two Hundred and Twenty Eighth Report of the
Committee. Action Taken notes on the recommendations of the Committee were received from the
Department on 20
th September, 2012.
The Committee’s recommendations, action taken thereon and comments of the Committee
on the Action Taken by the Department of Biotechnology are set out in the subsequent paragraphs:-
Recommendation (Para 4.4)
The Committee is happy to note that the Department has developed a strong and potent
monitoring mechanism and commends it for being amongst the best three Ministries/Departments
in the financial year 2010-11 in the Government’s performance review. The Committee hopes that
the Department would not only continue to maintain at least the same level of performance but
would also endeavour to perform even better in the Twelfth Five Year Plan.
Action Taken by Government
The Department while noting the appreciation by the Committee on the past performance,
would continue to perform as per directives given by the Committee through further strengthening
of project management and monitoring system.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply of the Department.
Recommendation (Para 5.3)
The Committee observes that from the year 2007-08 onwards there is no significant
variation between financial allocation in BE and RE stages. The utilization also ranges from
93.65 per cent in 2010-11 to as high as 99.17 per cent in 2008-09. These figures are indicative
of effective financial planning and robust monitoring of expenditure by the Department. The
Committee commends the excellent financial performance made by the Department and hopes that
the Department would even better this performance in the Twelfth Five Year Plan.
Action Taken by Government
The Department would continue perform in the direction suggested by the Committee
through further strengthening of project management and monitoring systems both in terms of
scientific and technical achievements and financial performance.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.

2
Recommendation (Para 5.5)
The Committee expresses satisfaction with the overall performance of the Department
during the Eleventh Plan period. The Committee is happy to know that technology transfer
agreements facilitated by DBT in Public-Private-Partnership (PPP) mode will ensure availability of
the world’s cheapest vaccines against Pneumococcal pneumonia, rotavirus, HPV, Chikungunya and
Japanese encephalitis. The Committee would further like the Department to make concerted efforts
to complete the clinical trials of vaccines for malaria, dengue, cholera and rotavirus at an early date
and make these vaccines available in the market as soon as possible.
Action Taken by Government
Under the DBT Public Private Partnership Programme on BIPP Industry Research
Programmes have been supported for development of affordable vaccines and the efforts for
clinical trial are continuing. The Rota virus project has completed the Phase-III trial and JE vaccine
has already obtained marketing license. The dengue vaccine candidate is under. pre-clinical studies.
The two malaria candidate vaccines developed by ICGEB completed phase-I clinical trial. The
Malaria Vaccine Development Programme (MVDP) established as an independent society is
overseeing the further development on malaria vaccine. The organization is being funded by DBT,
Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation, MVI, EMVI. Phase-III clinical trial of Cholera vaccine in human
subjects is in progress at NICED, Kolkata.
Comments
While appreciating the efforts made by the Department for development of vaccines
under Public Private Partnership mode, the Committee would like the Department to ensure
that results of these efforts become visible in near future with the availability of affordable
vaccines for the various diseases affecting the common man.
Recommendation (Para7.5)
The Committee expresses serious concern over the significant reduction of Rs.524.61
Crores between the Plan demand projected by the Department and the actual allocations made even
though Department maintains that it had projected reasonable demands. Due to this reduction in
allocation, the Department will need to re-prioritize allocation within various heads to initiate work
and will even have to defer some of the activities planned for that year to next year due to paucity
of funds. The Committee is of the view that considering the immense potential of Biotechnology
in providing affordable health care and increasing agricultural productivity as also India’s emergence
as one amongst the global leaders in biotechnology, adequate funds should be made available to the
Department so that our Research and Development activities are not adversely impacted. The
Committee, therefore, takes a very serious view of blind cuts made in the projected Demands of
the Department and recommends that the Government should provide adequate funds at R.E. stage
to the Department so that its important programmes and Research and Development activities are
vigorously pursued and our global competitiveness in biotechnology sector gets further
strengthened.
Action Taken by Government
The observations of the Committee have been taken-up with Planning Commission and
Department of Expenditure, Ministry of Finance. It was informed that Department may take-up the
additional demand for activities that could not be taken-up due to shortage of funds. Meanwhile,
DBT has entered into a collaboration with We llcome Trust, UK for development of affordable

3
healthcare products at a total cost of Rs. 330 crores with 50% contribution for each side. Several
such collaborations with international development agencies and countries have been agreed upon
in the areas of healthcare and agriculture which would offset the shortage of funds besides access
to advance technologies and training of young scientists.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and feels that the collaboration of the Department
with the various International development agencies/countries in the fields of healthcare
and agriculture is a step in the right direction as it would reduce dependence on the
Government for funding.
Recommendation (Para 8.5)
The Committee notes that the Plan allocation under the head of R&D for the year 2012-13
is to the tune of Rs. 455 crores which is significantly higher than B.E. Plan allocation of
Rs. 376.10 crores made in 2011-12. The Committee is of the view that higher allocation on R&D
are need of the hour and help India strengthen its position as one of the global leaders in
biotechnology.
Action Taken by Government
The Department has noted the views of the Committee for higher allocations to R&D.
Accordingly, the Department would take adequate steps for enhancing the allocation for R&D in
the subsequent years of Twelfth  Plan. The indicative budgetary allocation for Twelfth  Plan
communicated recently by Planning Commission is almost double the allocation of Eleventh Plan.
Therefore, the proposals of the Department in Twelfth Plan to launch major R&D programmes in
emerging areas such as system biology, synthetic biology, computation biology, RNAi biology and
nano-biotechnology would be adequately supported through increase in allocations and promote
R&D in universities and institutions to make India globally competitive in life sciences and
biotechnology.
Comments
The Committee takes note of the reply.
Recommendation (Para 9.4)
The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Government must ensure the functioning
of this important centre of research and quality of research being done there is not adversely
impacted due to reduction in financial allocation to the Centre and, if necessary, interim financial
assistance be provided to the Centre to tide over its immediate financial problems. The Committee
would also like the Centre to make concerted efforts so that it is able to meet its expenses from
its own income in a short time and it does not remain dependent on Government funds for its very
survival.
Action Taken by Government
Recognizing the significance of the observations of the Committee the Department of
Biotechnology, being the nodal agency of. ICGEB, New Delhi, is already holding elaborate
discussions with the ICGEB management and its governing body to work out a strategy and
modalities for support so as to address sustainability on long term. To tide over the current
situation, a special budget head has been introduced under the DBT plan budget of Twelfth Plan
in the scheme “support to autonomous R&D institutions” and the provision of Rs. 13.00 crores

4
has already been made for the year 2012-13. Out of which Rs. 650.00 lakhs has already been
released to ICGEB.
Comments
The Committee notes the opening of a separate budgetary head for autonomous R&D
institutions but reiterates that the Centre should make all out efforts to meet its expenses
from its own resources and should become self sustaining.
Recommendation (Para 10.2)
The Committee welcomes the decision to establish BIRAC with a view to support product
innovation and providing required infrastructure and services at different stages of the value chain
for promoting innovation and product development to public sector and private sectors through
facilitating bioindustrial growth. The Committee hopes that with the establishment of BIRAC, global
competitiveness of Indian biotech industry would increase and it would help us to increase our
market share in the global biotech products and services.
Action Taken by Government
BlRAC is now working closely with national and international agencies such as ICAR,
ICMR, DST, CSIR, Gates Foundation, WHO, World Bank to facilitate innovative product-orientated
research for development of affordable product and processes development. The required enabling
services such as Intellectual Property management, technology assessment, technology transfer,
legal and contractual agreements, processes for technology acquisition and licensing,
entrepreneurship development etc., are also being made available to facilitate the biotech industry
specially the startup’s and the SME’s.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply of the Department and hopes that concrete results
of establishment of BIRAC would soon become visible.
Recommendation (Para 11.2)
The Committee feels that quality human resources forms the backbone of research activities
in a country and as such the Department needs to accord greater priority to lapping, nurturing and
involving talented students in biotechnology. The Committee is of the opinion that the Department
must play a pro-active role in this regard. The Committee appreciates the efforts being made by the
Department in creating capable human resource in the biotechnology sector and extending support to
students at the college level through fellowships, short term training courses, providing industrial
training to B.Tech./M.Sc./M.Tech biotechnology students. The Committee also commends that the
Star College scheme initiated by the Department, which aims towards strengthening of life sciences,
biotechnology education and training and provides experience to biotechnology students in the cutting
edge-technologies needed for modern biological studies at undergraduate level in life sciences. The
Committee hopes that these schemes would help creating sufficient scientists and technocrats needed
by the expanding field of biotechnology. The Committee recommends that the Department should
carefully work our future requirements of human resources in the Biotechnology sector and, if
necessary, expand its existing schemes, to ensure availability of required manpower in years to come.
Action Taken by Government
The Department is encouraged of the views and appreciations made by the Committee on

5
the ongoing programmes and benefits that are expected to be realized. The Department has
internally assessed and also commissioned studies on human resource requirements in future. Some
areas identified from these efforts for special programmes in human resource development included:
Intellectual Property management, technology assessment, technology transfer, operation of GMP
and GLP facilities for production and services, high-end bioinformatics, computation biology,
system biology, synthetic biology, advance toxicology, biotech regulation and regulatory science etc.
During the Twelfth  Plan, to meet the needs of continuous assessment of human resource needs
and to manage the wide array of programmes, action has also been taken to establish a Life
Sciences and Biotechnology Education Agency.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and hopes that concrete benefits would flow from the
programmes undertaken by the Department.
Recommendation (Para 12.3)
The Committee, however, expresses its serious concern over inadequate allocation for R&D
purposes made by the private sector. Funding provided by the private sector in India is significantly
lower as compared to international norms of 1.3-1.4 of GDP. In France, Industry performs over
63 per cent (of all R&D) and funds around 54 per cent projects while this figure is 69 per cent
in Japan. In India, contribution of private sector industries is estimated at around 25 per cent
of national R&D expenditure which needs to be enhanced to at least 50 per cent in the Twelfth
Plan.
Action Taken by Government
The Department noted the observations of the Committee for enhancement of industry
contribution in R&D from the current level to up to 50 per cent. The efforts of the Department
for the first time to launch in 2007 the Small Business Innovative Research Initiative programme
of Public Private Partnership for promoting proof of concept R&D has provided significant results
invigorating the industry contribution. The scheme has benefited more than 100 small and medium
biotech enterprises at the total cost of Rs. 316 crores which includes 48 per cent of industry
contribution. Encouraged by this programme several steps have been taken in promoting industrial
R&D through various Public Private Partnerships schemes. The Biotechnology Industry Partnership
Programme (BIPP) launched has so far benefited 51 companies undertaking research in futuristic
high risk technologies at a total cost of Rs. 116 crores including 60 per cent of industry
contribution. Other programmes of the Department in Twelfth Plan already announced such as
ignition grants scheme, incubators and establishment of translational research platforms for product
development and other shared and expensive research facilities would further enhance the
contributioon of industry in R&D in life sciences and biotechnology.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply and hopes that the schemes launched by the
Department would lead to enhanced the share of the private sector for Research and
Development purposes.
Recommendation (Para 13.4)
The Committee appreciates the Department for taking initiatives for encouraging youth
across various streams of Biotechnology through a range of scholarships such as Wellcome Trust

6
Fellowship, Rapid Young Grant scheme, etc. The Committee also commends introduction of
Ramalingaswami Fellowships aimed at attracting Indian scientists coming back to their mother land
and hopes that schemes like this will help check brain-drain.
Action Taken by Government
The Department remains encouraged for the appreciation by the Committee on the
programmes for preventing brain drain. As per the directives of the Committee, all the programmes
with enhanced numbers of fellowships shall be continued during the Twelfth Plan.
To maintain transparency and standards, all the schemes are advertised every year in
national dailies, science magazines both at national and international level (Current Sciences,
Biospectrum, Technology Review, Nature, Science) and applications are invited from candidates
across the world.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply.
Recommendation (Para 13.5)
The Committee, however, would like the Department to follow a transparent and objective
criterion for award of these scholarships/fellowships so that only deserving and talented persons
get them. The Committee would also like the Department to devise ways and means so that talented
students coming from rural background, belonging to deprived sections of society and women
scholars could also be encouraged to join the stream of Biotechnology.
Action Taken by Government
The applications received are scrutinized by a high level expert committee duly constituted
by the Department. Track record of applicant such as work experience after Ph.D/MD/equivalent
degree; Awards/Honors-National/International, Extramural research grants raised during the last
five years — National/International; Number of Patents/Varieties/Hybrids; Technologies developed;
Number of first author papers published during 5 years; Number of papers in which
the candidate is the corresponding author; quality and impact of publications; Scientific merit of
the research proposal to be carried out during the tenure for the fellowship; Comments/
Recommendations of the Host Institute, the overall assessment on the suitability of the candidate
for this award.
The Department has initiated a Biocare scheme for providing research grant opportunity to
women scientists who have not received research grant earlier. This is mainly to help women
scientists to be able to undertake independent research programme for enhancing their capacities
and giving them an opportunity to work with mentors and establish research institutes in
scientifically important research area. Similarly, the Department has scheme for biotechnology based
programmes for rural development and SC/ST population under which several training programmes
are conducted for the purpose. As suggested by the committee action has been taken to strengthen
these efforts.
Comments
The Committee takes note of the reply. The Committee would like the Department
to carry periodic review of its schemes and commission an independent study to assess  the
actual benefits flowing from its schemes.

7
Recommendation (Para 14.4)
The Committee appreciates the fact the Department has been contributing to societal
development by making use of biotechnology processes and tools and notes that during Eleventh
Five Year Plan, 4500 rural, SC/ST and women were benefited from this programme. The
Committee is of the view that Department should expand its programme significantly to provide for
skill development, employment and income generation in the field of agriculture, sericulture, etc.
The Committee, also feels, that the Department should particularly focus on extending help to Self
Help Groups, Cooperatives etc. so that larger number of people could be benefited from its
programmes. The Department must also try to focus finding innovative opportunities for income
generation by using biotechnology tools and processes on locally available resources.
Action Taken by Government
As suggested by the Committee, division has expanded its activities/programmes on skill
development, employment and income generation in the field of agriculture, sericulture etc. The
priority of the programme area has been set well  leading to the promotion of agro-technologies with
introduction of hybrids, new crops, disease/stress resistant varieties. Project activities are also
supported for  integrated farming through introduction of animal husbandry, horticulture and various
other allied activities. Emphasis was given on utilization of local bio-resources in a  sustainable and
eco-friendly manner through SHGs and entrepreneurship development and also focusing on creation
of innovative opportunities in different income  generation activities using biotechnological tools
through utilization of local bio-resources.
Comments
The Committee appreciates the initiative taken by the Department to uplift weaker
segment of the Society using Biotechnological tools and processes and hopes that concrete
results would flow in the near future from the programmes launched by the Department.
Recommendation (Para 15.3)
The Committee is happy to note that introduction of break-up of budget will not adversely
impact this programme. The Committee considers the programme as of great importance for
common man and would like the Department to make all out efforts to ensure that the programme
achieves its objectives. The Committee would particularly like the Department to ensure that
cheaper vaccines for ailments of common man become quickly available in the market.
Action Taken by Government
The suggestions made by the Committee have been noted. During the year 2012-2013,
based on past experience and actual assessment of requirements, care has been taken to
rationalize the break-up of budget into capital cost (non-recurring) and grant-in-aid (recurring) so
that such mandatory breakup may have minimal impact on implementation of the programmes.
For effective translational research of healthcare and agriculture products, Department during the
year 2012-2013 has already operationalised following platforms which would accelerate various
steps in product development. These platforms include clinical development and service agency
for human vaccines and diagnostic, platform for veterinary biological for animal vaccines and
development.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply. The Committee, however, would like the Department

8
to ensure that its efforts actually result in development of affordable healthcare and
agriculture products, in a fixed time-frame, which may benefit the common man.
Recommendation (Para 16.6)
The Committee would like the Department to pursue with the Planning Commission and
Ministry of Finance for allocation of higher funds for this programme at the RE stage 2012-13 so
that the objective of establishment of new Centres of Excellence in life Sciences, Biotechnology and
Bioinformatics during 2012-13, as originally planned by the Department could be achieved. The
Committee recommends Ministry of Finance and Planning Commission to make sufficient funds
available for establishment of sufficient number of Centres of Excellence for carrying out research
in advance and cutting-edge areas of Biotechnology and Bioinformatics so that country not only
maintains its competitive edge in Biotechnology but further strengthens it.
Action Taken by Government
The Department has taken up the suggestions of the Committee with Planning Commission
during the discussions for finalization of Twelfth Plan budget. Adequate justification was given for
higher allocation to promote important programmes such as centres of excellence in cutting edge
areas of life science and biotechnology. Accordingly, the indicative budgetary allocation for Twelfth
Plan communicated recently by Planning Commission is almost double from the allocation of
Eleventh Plan. This would facilitate to implement the proposals of the Department in the Eleventh
Plan to setup more centres of excellence, inter-institutional centres, Advance centre for
bioinformatics and computation biology and DBT partnership centres in leading areas of global
importance. Already action has been taken for preparation of five such proposals.
Comments
The Committee is happy to note that the Department has got an indicative budgetary
allocation almost double to the allocation of the Eleventh Plan which would help setting up
of more Centres of excellence, and Bioinformatics centres which it hopes would be gainfully
utilised.
Recommendation (Para 17.3)
The Committee welcomes the step taken by the Department to merge the schemes with
overlapping mandates particularly as it would provide larger scope for implementation of more
programmes. The Committee also feels that special attention needs to be given to promote
women scientists to forefront in order to bring gender equality in the field of biotechnology.
All women Biotech Park can be a step in this direction. The Committee recommends that under
the head of I&M Sector considerable investment should be made in collaboration with private
sector for setting up of more women’s Biotechnology parks in other areas of the country such
as in Jammu and Kashmir which is having considerable number of women Muslim science
graduates.
Action Taken by Government
The Department has initiated a Bio-care scheme for providing research grant opportunity to
women scientists who have not received research grant earlier. This is mainly to help women
scientists to be able to undertake independent research programme for enhancing their capacities
and giving them an opportunity to work with mentors and establish research institutes in
scientifically important research area.

9
The Department is already implementing 22 R&D programmes relevant to the needs of J&K
State. Some major initiatives include participation in network programme to improve apple and
saffron. A repository on apple germ plasma has also been supported. Five slots in the DBT
overseas fellowship scheme have been reserved for the applicants of the State. As suggested by
the Committee, a meeting to explore possibilities of strengthening life science and biotechnology
programmes has been scheduled in the month of October 2012. Secretary, DBT along with key
officials of the Department are participating. All the heads of institutions and universities from the
State of J&K are participating in the meeting.
Comments
The Committee notes that the Department is implementing twenty-two R&D
programmes relevant to the needs of Jammu and Kashmir State and would like Department
to get the actual benefits flowing from these programmes to the State of Jammu and
Kashmir assessed by an independent agency.
Recommendation (Para 18.6)
The Committee feels that huge investment needed in Science and Technology research can
only be mobilized by introducing significant changes in current interaction of publicly owned S&T
establishment with industry both in public and private sectors. The Committee feels that if India
has to emerge as a scientifically developed nation, private sector investment in Science and
Technology has to increase substantially from the present levels and Public Private Partnership can
prove to be a great source of resource mobilization.
Recommendation (Para 18.7)
After going through the details of SBIRI and BIPP programmes, the Committee is of the
opinion that these are well intended and useful programmes. It notes that BIPP has diverse
components covering health, environment and industry, etc. and the utility of the scheme stands
established by breakthrough research concepts which have already led to commercialization of
various projects benefiting 51 companies apart from leading to development of H1N1 vaccine which
was recently approved by Drug Controller General of India (DCGI) for marketing. The Committee
strongly recommends that this scheme must continue during the Twelfth Plan as proposed by the
Department since such investment may; bring out sea change in the entire scenario of health,
environment and industry combined.
Action Taken by Government
During the Twelfth Plan all the public private partnership schemes (SBIRI and BIPP) shall
be continued with improved administrative and governance to accelerate the process of funding and
management. In addition, a new PPP scheme such as ignition grants, technology incubators, setting
up of shared infrastructure facilities will also be implemented to promote overall development of
R&D and innovation in biotech industry.
Comments
The Committee is pleased to learn that both SBIRI and BIPP programmes would be
continued during the Twelfth Plan period also. The Committee hopes that the Department
would further encourage other private sector Companies to join Public Private Partnership
mode of funding for R&D and innovation in biotech industry.

10
Recommendations (Para 19.3 and 19.4)
The Committee is happy at increased international collaboration with various countries. The
committee notes that there has been an increase of allocation amounting of Rs. 8.50 crores under
this head. Mutually beneficial international collaboration in the field of Biotechnology needs to be
encouraged so as to boost the pace of progress and growth in the key areas of Biotechnology and
recommends accordingly.
The Committee is particularly happy at the result of international collaboration under
Biodesign Alliance Programme being run with the support of the Stanford University, USA. The
Committee notes that DBT has been able to mobilize through international collaborations funding to
the tune of Rs. 1000 crores out of which National Institute of Health (NIH), USA and Wellcome
Trust, UK have contributed 50 per cent of the money. The Committee, therefore, recommends that
in view of the mutually beneficial potential of international collaborations in Biotechnology, increase
in allocation beyond Rs. 8.50 crores be made in the subsequent years of Twelfth Five Year Plan
so as to adequately fund the programme.
Action Taken by Government
The budget allocated for international collaboration is basically meant for providing seed
money for launching of programmes meeting expenditure on travel, workshops and conferences
and R&D in bilateral projects costing up to Rs. 2.00 crores. Wherever collaborations require major
investments, the provision is made out of the other relevant operational schemes under the budget
heads such as R&D and I&M Sector. For example the contribution for W ellcome Trust DBT
partnerships as well as biodesign are met out of sub budget head “Medical Biotechnology and
Related Areas” of the scheme ‘Research and Development’. Similarly, major investment required for
agriculture R&D collaborations are budgeted under the sub head “Agriculture Biotechnology and
Allied Areas” of the scheme of ‘Research and Development’. Since the indicative budget outlay for
Twelfth Plan is substantial, as suggested by the committee the allocation will be increased under
the head “International Collaboration” during the subsequent years of the Twelfth  Plan.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply of the Department and hopes that international
collaborations will help boost growth in the key areas of Biotechnology.
Recommendation (Para 20.6)
The Committee is happy to note that the programme is bringing positive transformation in
North Eastern states and Sikkim. Keeping in view of the good performance of the programme, the
committee not only feels that mandatory 10 percent allocation should continue for the programme
but budgetary allocations to the extent possible should be leveraged to bring more funds in North
Eastern states through PPP mode for biotechnology applications. The Department should also Plan
towards cooperation with other scientific Departments to boost pace of growth in this region. The
Committee, further, wants the Department to explore that possibility of earmarking certain percent
mandatory allocation for other backward regions of the country such as the Himalayan Region as
well.
Action Taken by Government
As suggested by the Committee, the Department has taken action to implement several
industry oriented and entrepreneurship development programmes in the north-east to promote public
private partnership. The ongoing programmes are already implemented through active involvement

11
of ICAR, CSIR and DST along with state Government agencies and S&T Council. As suggested
by the Committee such collaboration will be strengthened further to avoid duplication and bring
value addition.
To explore the possibility of earmarking certain per cent mandatory allocation for other
backward regions in life sciences and biotechnology, Department has constituted the Committee to
work-out the strategy and programmes for implementation in 2013-2014.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply of the Department and hopes that the Department
will ensure that Himalayan, North-eastern and other backward regions of the country get
benefited by its proposed projects.
Recommendation (Para 20.7)
The Committee commends the fact that in successive years the Department has been able
to utilize the progressively increasing allocations in Plan outlays. The Committee also notes that the
Department has been able to utilize an amount of Rs. 1376.70 crores, out of total allotted 1426.92
crores in the year 2011-12. For the financial year 2012-13 period, it is hoped that the Department
will be able to optimally utilize the total outlay of Rs. 1500.39 crores. After considering the
Demands for Grants of the Department of Biotechnology, the Committee is of the view of that the
Department of Biotechnology, by and large, is making good use of the public money and hopes
that the Department would continue making proper use of public funds in future also.
Action Taken by Government
The Department is encouraged of the appreciation made by the Committee for its financial
performance and the recommendation made for 2012-2013. The views of the Committee on making
good use of the public money has been communicated to all divisions and task forces of DBT for
implementation.
Comments
The Committee notes the reply of the Department and hopes that the Department
would make unwavering efforts to fulfill the goals set for the Twelfth Five Year Plan.

REPORT 
 
  INTRODUCTION 
1.  The Department of Atomic Energy that made a modest beginning in the year 1954 
with the primary objective of harnessing nuclear energy to meet the energy requirements 
of the country, has in its about  fifty eight years of  journey, mostly so litary dotted with 
international sanctions and technology denials, carved out a niche for itself in the arena of 
Atomic Energy.  Starting with a specifi c mandate of energy generation, it has 
successfully diversified and multiplied its activi ties in a number of socially relevant and 
useful programmes, projects and disciplines.  The current mandate of the Department, on 
which its programmes are based extends to:- 
 Increasing share of nuclear power through deployment of indigenous and 
other proven technologies, along with de velopment of fast breeder reactors 
and thorium reactors with associated fuel cycle facilities; 
 Building and operation of research reactors for production of radioisotopes 
and carrying out radiation technology appl ications in the fi eld of medicine, 
agriculture and industry; 
 Developing advanced technologies  such as accelerators, lasers, 
supercomputers, advanced materials a nd instrumentation, and encouraging 
transfer of technology to industry. 
 Support to basic research in nuclear energy and related frontier areas of 
science; interaction with universities and academic institutions; Support to 
research and development projects ha ving a bearing in DAE’s programmes, 
and international cooperation in related advanced areas of research; and 
 Contribution to national security.   
Some of the significant deliverables from Department of Atomic Energy include:  
 Energy Security 
 National Security 
 Food security 
 Water security 

 Health security 
 Bringing-in benefits of Nuclear and Ra diation Technologies for the growth of 
Indian industries 
 Cancer research 
 National capacity building through pr omotion of science education and 
research  
2.  While, we have enough reasons to cheer the impressive and commendable 
achievements and feel proud of the advancem ents made by the Department of Atomic 
Energy, we need to guard ourselves from the danger of becoming complacent by basking 
in the past and the present glory. The Depart ment of Atomic Energy has miles to go and 
many milestones to achieve.  It is yet to re alize its vision to empower India through 
technology, create more wealth and provide bett er quality of life to  its citizens, make 
India energy independent, contri bute to provision of sufficien t, safe and nutritious food 
and better healthcare to our people through de velopment and deployment of nuclear and 
radiation technologies and their applicatio ns. Even after, over four decades of 
commercial operation of nuclear power plants, the Department of Atomic Energy is yet to 
redeem the dream of three stage nuclear pow er programme conceived by Dr. Bhabha, the 
precursor of atomic energy in the country.  We have hitherto been able to master only the 
first of the three stage nuclear power programme.  The share of nuclear in total electricity 
generation is mere a dismal 3.7 per cent (approx .) with a total inst alled capacity of 4,780 
MW.   
3. All this, notwithstanding, the greatest st rength of Indian Nuclear Programme lies 
in its major strides towards self-reliance a nd indigenous research and development both 
in power and non-power application being the outcome of multi-disciplinary, multi-
institutional and multi-dimensional prog rammes undertaken by the Department of 
Atomic Energy in an era marked by international sanctions and technology denials.   
4.  The Department of Atomic Energy, over th e years, has established a vast network 
of institutions and evolved a broad based organisation to support,  sustain and carry 
forward its avowed objec tives and activities.  It has, so far, esta blished 107 installations 
spread across several States of the country.  The Organisations/Institutions under the 
ambit of Department of Atomic Energy, category-wise, are as follows:- 
 Research Centres:  Bhabha Atomic Research  Centre (BARC)– Mumbai; 
Indira Gandhi Centre for Atomic Re search (IGCAR)– Kalpakkam; Raja 
Ramanna Centre for Advanced Technology (RRCAT)– Indore; Variable 
Energy Cyclotron Centre (VECC)– Kolkata; and Atomic Minerals Directorate 
for Exploration and Research (AMD) – Hyderabad; Global Centre for Nuclear 
Energy Partnership (GCNEP), Gurgaon. 
 Industrial Organisations:  Heavy Water Board (HWB) – Mumbai; Nuclear 
Fuel Complex (NFC)– Hyderabad; a nd Board of Radiation and Isotope 
Technology (BRIT)– Mumbai.  
 Service Organisations:  Directorate of Purchase  & Stores (DPS)– Mumbai, 
Directorate of Construction, Services  and Estate Management (DCSEM)– 
Mumbai; and General Services Organisation (GSO)– Kalpakkam.   
 Public Sector Undertakings:  Nuclear Power Corpor ation of India Ltd. 
(NPCIL)– Mumbai; Bharatiya Nabhiki ya Vidyut Nigam Ltd. (BHAVINI); 
Kalpakkam, Tamil Nadu; Uranium Co rporation of India Ltd. (UCIL)– 

Jaduguda; Indian Rare Earths Ltd. (IREL)– Mumbai; and Electronics 
Corporation of India Ltd. (ECIL)– Hyderabad.  
 Aided Institutions:  Tata Institute of Fundame ntal Research (TIFR) – 
Mumbai; Tata Memorial Centre (TMC) – Mumbai; Saha Inst itute of Nuclear 
Physics (SINP) – Kolkata; Institute of Physics (IOP) – Bhubaneswar; National 
Institute of Science Education and Research (NISER) – Bhubaneswar; Harish-
Chandra Research Institute (HRI) – A llahabad; Institute of Mathematical 
Sciences (IMSc) – Chennai; Institu te for Plasma Research (IPR) – 
Ahmedabad; and Atomic Energy Education Society (AEES) – Mumbai. 
 DAE through Board of Research in Nu clear Sciences (BRNS) and National 
Board for Higher Mathematics (NBHM) Promotes research in nuclear and 
allied fields and mathematics, respectively.   
 Academic programmes run by BARC, IGCAR, RRCAT, VECC, SINP, IPR, 
IOP NISER, IMSc, HRI and TMC come under the fold of Homi Bhabha 
National Institute, a deemed University.  TIFR is also a deemed university.  
5.  Grants for Department of Atomic Energy
 
5.1  There are two Grants, i.e., Grant No. 4 (Atomic Energy) and Grant No. 5 (Nuclear 
Power Schemes) under which Demands for Grants  of the Department of Atomic Energy 
are made.  Grants for six research Centres, three industrial Organi sations, three Public 
Sector Undertakings; Aided In stitutions; three Service Orga nisations; Atomic Energy 
Regulatory Board (AERB), etc. are covered under Grant No. 4.  Grant No. 5 comprises of 
Budgetary allocations mainly for Nuclear Power Corporation of India Ltd. and BHAVINI 
besides Bhabha Atomic Research Centre fo r Waste Water Management facilities and 
Indira Gandhi Centre for Atomic Research for Prototype Fast Breeder Test Reactor, etc.   
6.  Projected vis-à-vis Approved XII Fi ve Year Plan Outlay – A Comparison

8.  Utilisation of XI Five Year Budgetary Outlay  
8.1  It is pertinent to  point out here that the approved outlay for a Five Year Plan does 
not in any way guarantee that the Department  would actually get and utilize the entire 
allocated amount during the span of five financ ial years.  On an analysis of the overall 
financial summary of the Department of Atom ic Energy pertaining to XI Five Year Plan 
reveals that out of the total approved ou tlay of Rs. 46431.13 Crores, the Actual for the 
first 4 years, i.e., 2007-08 to 2010-11 remained  at Rs. 21916.94 Crores.  Even in the last 
year, it was tentatively expected that the expenditure/ utilisati on would extend to Rs. 
31811.49 Crores during the entire XI  Plan period.  But finally, it got restricted to Rs. 
29173.00 Crores.  If the total Budgetary allocati on of the XI Five Year Plan i.e. Rs. 
46431.13 Crores is distributed evenly among the five financial years, the average 
allocation per year works out tentatively to  Rs. 9000.00 Crores.  The actual utilization 

being restricted only to the extent of Rs. 29173.00 Crores suggests that the Budgetary 
resources adequate to meet the allocation fo r two financial years remained unutilized.  
Thus out of the five years, it can also be said  that there was nil or zero utilisation for two 
financial years. Going by this rate of utilisa tion, it could not be claimed that the outlay of 
Rs. 107186.73 Crores approved for the XII Five Year Plan would be fully utilized.

11. Impact of cut in Non-Plan Allocation
 
11.1  The Committee has been informed th at reduction in propos ed demand under the 
Non-Plan Head for Demand No. 4 by Rs. 957. 22 Crores would have an adverse impact 
on nuclear power generation and other related areas.  Heavy Water Plants, Nuclear Fuel 
Complex etc., will function in a reduced capacity as they are already carrying the liability 
of spillover payment of Rs. 376.00 Crores on account of raw materials,  utilities by 
Heavy Water Plant, Nuclea r Fuel Complex and BARC from 2012-13 because of the 
shortfall in the Non-Plan outlay in the y ear 2012-13.  This year, cut will lead to a 
cascading effect of additional burden on them.  It was further informed that the budget 
shortfall will also have adverse impact on th e upkeep of some very old laboratories and 
facilities of R&D Units and fully aided institutions. The Department further informed that 
owing to the shortfall in the Non-Plan allocat ion last year, Uranium Corporation of India 
Ltd. had to resort to a corporate loan of Rs . 100.00 Crores as it could not get the payment 
from Nuclear Fuel Complex for the supplies made by them.  It was also brought to the 
notice of the Committee that in the previo us financial year they had made some 
arrangements but in the current financial ye ar, they must get the additional resources.  
The Department further informed that unde r Grant No. 5 for fuel inventory, the 

Department had projected a demand of Rs. 3314.00 Crores under Non-Plan, but an outlay 
of only Rs.2471.68 Crores has been approved.  The Committee takes note of the serious 
concerns expressed by the Department and the adverse effect that the reduced allocation 
would have both on the Atomic Energy Pr ogramme, as well as, on Nuclear Power 
Schemes.   
11.2  The Committee is of the vi ew that Nuclear Fuel Complex and Heavy Water Plants 
form the core of Nuclear Power Programme  and hence such critical and important 
schemes of the Department, must not be made to suffer for want of funds.  The 
Committee had in its 222
nd Report on the Demands for Grants 2012-13 too, 
recommended that Non-Plan allocation be suitably enhanced at RE Stage in order to 
avoid adverse impacts arising out of reduction of Non-Plan allocation.  The Department 
of Atomic Energy, had in its Action Taken Report, informed the Committee that the 
Ministry of Finance had assured that Department’s requirements will be considered 
favourably at RE Stage.  The Committee finds  that in pursuance of its recommendations 
made in its 222
nd Report, the Ministry of Finance ha d increased the Non-Plan allocation 
both for Nuclear Fuel Complex and Heavy Water Board from BE  1105.28 Crores and 
701.04 Crores respectively to Rs. 1333.94 Crores and Rs. 814.36 Crores respectively, 
amounting to a total increase of Rs. 341.98 Cror es under Grant No. 4.   Under Grant No. 
5, while the BE Non-Plan allocations fo r Fuel Inventory and Heavy Water Pool 
Management was Rs. 2400.00 Crores and Rs. 99 0.00 Crores respectively, the former was 
increased to Rs. 2450.01 Crores while the la tter remained unchanged.  Thus the total 
increase under these Heads at the RE stage amounts to Rs. 391.99 Cror es.  Last year, the 
Department had emphasised on the restoration of  shortfall in Non-Pl an allocation to the 
extent of Rs. 984.67 Crores in Demand No. 4 and the shortfall of Rs. 377.94 Crores in 
Demand No. 5, thus asking for restoration of Non-Plan allocation to the extent of Rs. 
1362.61 Crores.  It becomes obvious that the in crease in the allocati on at the RE stage 
was not commensurate to the Demand of the Department and the Ministry of Finance 
heeded the recommendation of the Committee onl y partially.  The Department of Atomic 
Energy this year also has raised the issue of  restoration of Non-Pl an expenditure, despite 
the fact it has not been able to fully utilise  the revised budgetary allocation of the year 
2012-13.  The Committee, therefore, recommends that while the Department of 
Atomic Energy should ensure full utilisat ion of allocated budgetary resources and 
should ask for additional funds only when it is in a position to utilise additional 
funds  asked for by it.  The Committee al so recommends that Ministry of Finance 
should adequately accommodate the dema nd of the Ministry to obviate adverse 
effects on the critical or core activities of the Department due to shortage of funds.
